```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())

library(tidyverse)
library(vcfR)
library(ggpubr)
library(patchwork)
library(scales)

theme_set(theme_classic())
```

This notebook follows the variants that Mutect2 calls
outside the known CHIP positions ("non-CHIP variants") across the serial samples of each participant,
compares them with the CHIP variants, and ends with the limit of detection (LoD) of these variants
calculated with the `chip_lod` package.

| Section | Step |
|---|---|
| 1 | Data: Mutect2 calls of all samples, sample dates |
| 2 | **Defining CHIP and non-CHIP variants** |
| 3 | bam-readcount pileup at the variant positions, one row per sample and variant |
| 4 | **Splitting non-CHIP variants into potential germline and potential somatic** |
| 5 | **Comparing Mutect2 with bam-readcount** |
| 6 | **Exploring non-CHIP variants and comparing them with CHIP variants** |
| 7 | **Limit of detection of non-CHIP variants (`chip_lod`)**, with a stringent set of somatic trajectories (7.6) |
| 8 | **Theoretical LoD and the data**: figures and numbers for the paper (SHCS and SardiNIA) |
| 9 | Differences from an earlier version of this notebook |

Terms used throughout:

- **call**: one Mutect2 record in one sample.
- **variant**: `CHROM_POS_REF_ALT` (column `variant`).
- **trajectory**: one variant in one individual across that individual's timepoints (column `traj_id`).

The notebook writes three outputs, each only if its parameter is set to `TRUE`; everything else is only read:

- the two region lists for bam-readcount (`write_region_files`, to new file names, see section 2.3);
- the contamination check of every sample, `resources/SHCS_sample_contamination_QC.txt` (`write_sample_qc`,
  section 3.3). `02_SHCS_CHIP_trajectories.Rmd` and `03_nonCHIP_variants_QC.Rmd` read it to
  leave out the samples flagged as mixed;
- the four panels of Figure S2 and their assembly, as png and svg, to `output/Supplementary_Figures/`
  (`write_paper_figures`, section 8).


# Parameters

```{r parameters}
chip_vaf <- 0.02             # CHIP VAF threshold, dashed line in the plots

# potential germline vs potential somatic
het_af_range <- c(0.3, 0.6)  # all calls of a trajectory inside this range: heterozygous germline
hom_af_min   <- 0.9          # any call above: homozygous germline
low_af_max   <- 0.2          # "low VAF" limit used for single calls and for the pileup median VAF

mixed_sample_min   <- 0.01      # sample flagged as mixed above this share of foreign reads (section 3.3)
pileup_ratio_range <- c(0.5, 2) # pileup / Mutect2 variant reads of a variant; outside: not followed in the pileup (5.1)
max_individuals    <- 5         # a variant found in more individuals than this is recurrent (section 7.6)

# One sample is in the pileup twice, under two suffixed names (section 3.1: the two
# runs hold the same reads). resources/pileup_sample_names.txt lists the run to use and the run to drop
# (tab-separated: pileup_name, action = use / drop, sample)
pileup_names <- read.delim("resources/pileup_sample_names.txt", colClasses = "character")
pileup_sample_alias <- with(subset(pileup_names, action == "use"), setNames(sample, pileup_name))
pileup_sample_drop  <- subset(pileup_names, action == "drop")$pileup_name

# the example individuals of sections 5.3 and 6.2, by their participant id in the paper
paper_ids <- read.delim("resources/SHCS_change_ids.txt")
id_of <- function(new_id) paper_ids$ID[paper_ids$SHCS_ID_new == new_id]

# chip_lod (package defaults)
err_rate  <- 0.001           # per-base sequencing error rate e
alpha     <- 0.05            # per-site false-positive rate used for k*
power_tgt <- 0.95            # detection probability that defines the LoD

write_region_files <- TRUE  # TRUE writes the bam-readcount region lists of section 2.3
write_sample_qc    <- TRUE  # TRUE writes the per-sample contamination table of section 3.3
write_paper_figures <- TRUE # TRUE writes the figures of section 8 (png and svg) to paper_fig_dir

paper_dir     <- "output"
paper_fig_dir <- file.path(paper_dir, "Supplementary_Figures")

chip_colors   <- c("non-CHIP" = "#F8766D", "CHIP" = "#00BFC4")
class_colors  <- c("potential somatic" = "#D55E00", "potential germline" = "grey55")
status_levels <- c("VAF >= LoD", "called, VAF < LoD", "not called (k < k*)")
status_colors <- setNames(c("#2a78d6", "#E69F00", "#898781"), status_levels)

med_iqr <- function(x, digits = 0, scale = 1) {
  if (all(is.na(x))) return("-")
  q <- quantile(x * scale, c(0.5, 0.25, 0.75), na.rm = TRUE)
  sprintf("%.*f (%.*f-%.*f)", digits, q[1], digits, q[2], digits, q[3])
}
n_pct <- function(x) sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", sum(x), 100 * mean(x))
```


# 1. Data

## 1.1 Mutect2 calls

One single-sample VCF per sequenced sample. From each record the sample fields `GT`, `AD` (reference and
alternate read counts), `AF` and `DP` are kept.

```{r read-mutect2}
vcf_dir   <- "resources/mutect2_Calls/mutect2_output"
vcf_files <- list.files(vcf_dir, pattern = "vcf.gz$")

# One row per record of a single-sample Mutect2 VCF
read_mutect2_vcf <- function(file) {
  vcf <- read.vcfR(file.path(vcf_dir, file), verbose = FALSE)
  stopifnot(ncol(vcf@gt) == 2)                       # FORMAT + one sample
  fmt <- function(element) unname(extract.gt(vcf, element = element)[, 1])
  ad  <- str_split_fixed(fmt("AD"), ",", 3)          # "ref,alt" (more alleles only at multiallelic sites)

  as_tibble(vcf@fix[, c("CHROM", "POS", "REF", "ALT", "FILTER"), drop = FALSE]) %>%
    mutate(Sample    = colnames(vcf@gt)[2],
           POS       = as.integer(POS),
           GT        = fmt("GT"),
           ref_count = as.numeric(ad[, 1]),
           alt_count = as.numeric(ad[, 2]),
           AF        = as.numeric(str_split_fixed(fmt("AF"), ",", 2)[, 1]),
           DP        = as.numeric(fmt("DP")))
}

mutect_all <- map_dfr(vcf_files, read_mutect2_vcf)
```

Records that Mutect2 flags as `germline` or `multiallelic` are removed, as are calls on chrY. Everything
else is kept, so the table holds `PASS` calls and calls with other Mutect2 filter flags.

```{r filter-mutect2}
mutect_all %>%
  mutate(record = case_when(
    grepl("germline|multiallelic", FILTER) ~ "removed: FILTER contains germline or multiallelic",
    CHROM == "chrY"                        ~ "removed: chrY",
    FILTER == "PASS"                       ~ "kept: PASS",
    TRUE                                   ~ "kept: other Mutect2 filter flags")) %>%
  count(record, name = "records") %>%
  knitr::kable()

merged_vcf <- mutect_all %>%
  filter(!grepl("germline|multiallelic", FILTER), CHROM != "chrY")

# AD is "ref,alt" and adds up to DP in every kept record
stopifnot(all(merged_vcf$ref_count + merged_vcf$alt_count == merged_vcf$DP))
```

Filter flags of the kept calls that are not `PASS` (a call can carry several):

```{r filter-flags}
merged_vcf %>%
  filter(FILTER != "PASS") %>%
  separate_rows(FILTER, sep = ";") %>%
  count(flag = FILTER, name = "calls", sort = TRUE) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

Number of kept calls per sample:

```{r calls-per-sample, fig.height=3.5}
merged_vcf %>%
  count(Sample) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Sample, y = n)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = paste0("Sample (", n_distinct(merged_vcf$Sample), ")"), y = "Mutect2 calls kept") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
```


## 1.2 Samples

Sample manifest with the collection date of each sample. Age at collection is the collection year minus
the SHCS birth year. `has_vcf` marks the samples with a Mutect2 VCF.

```{r samples}
admin <- read.csv("resources/SHCS_database/2025-12/admin.csv") %>%
  distinct(ID, BORN)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(admin$ID))

samples <- read.csv("resources/samples_with_dates.csv") %>%
  transmute(Sample  = ID,
            ID      = as.numeric(gsub("ID SHCS ", "", Subject.Id)),
            LABDATE = as.Date(gsub(" 00:00:00", "", Collection), format = "%d/%m/%Y")) %>%
  left_join(admin, by = "ID") %>%
  mutate(Age     = as.integer(format(LABDATE, "%Y")) - BORN,
         has_vcf = Sample %in% sub(".vcf.gz$", "", vcf_files)) %>%
  select(-BORN)

merged_vcf <- merged_vcf %>%
  inner_join(samples, by = "Sample")
stopifnot(n_distinct(merged_vcf$Sample) == length(vcf_files))

# individuals with longitudinal sequencing (a Mutect2 VCF)
long_ids <- sort(unique(merged_vcf$ID))

samples %>%
  filter(has_vcf) %>%
  count(ID, name = "timepoints") %>%
  count(timepoints, name = "individuals") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Timepoints with a Mutect2 VCF per individual")
```


# 2. Defining CHIP and non-CHIP variants

## 2.1 CHIP positions

The CHIP variants are the calls made at Vanderbilt (`CHIP_calls_all_long.csv`, ANNOVAR coordinates).

```{r chip-list}
chip_calls_long <- read.csv("resources/CHIP_calls_longitudinal/CHIP_calls_all_long.csv", fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM") %>%
  distinct(Gene = Gene.refGene, Chr, Start, End, Ref, Alt, Func.refGene, ExonicFunc.refGene, AAChange.refGene)

c(CHIP_variants = nrow(chip_calls_long), positions = nrow(distinct(chip_calls_long, Chr, Start)))
```

A VCF and ANNOVAR do not describe an indel with the same position and alleles, and bam-readcount follows
the ANNOVAR convention:

| | VCF (Mutect2) | ANNOVAR / bam-readcount |
|---|---|---|
| SNV | `POS`, `REF>ALT` | same position, allele `ALT` |
| deletion | `chr17:60663171 TA>T` | `Start = 60663172`, `Ref = A`, `Alt = -`, allele `-A` |
| insertion | `chr4:105272692 G>GA` | `Start = 105272692`, `Ref = -`, `Alt = A`, allele `+A` |

`get_variant_locus()` converts a VCF variant to this convention.

```{r variant-locus}
# VCF (POS, REF, ALT) -> locus and alleles as used by ANNOVAR and bam-readcount.
#   rc_pos, rc_end : first and last position of the locus (region for bam-readcount)
#   rc_allele      : allele string in the bam-readcount output ("A", "+A", "-A")
get_variant_locus <- function(pos, ref, alt) {
  ref <- toupper(ref)
  alt <- toupper(alt)

  if (nchar(ref) == nchar(alt)) {
    return(tibble(type = ifelse(nchar(ref) == 1, "SNV", "MNV"),
                  rc_pos = pos, rc_end = pos + nchar(ref) - 1,
                  annovar_ref = ref, annovar_alt = alt, rc_allele = alt))
  }

  # strip shared leading bases beyond the single VCF anchor base
  while (nchar(ref) > 1 && nchar(alt) > 1 && substr(ref, 1, 1) == substr(alt, 1, 1)) {
    ref <- substr(ref, 2, nchar(ref))
    alt <- substr(alt, 2, nchar(alt))
    pos <- pos + 1
  }

  if (nchar(alt) > nchar(ref)) {
    # insertion: stays at the anchor position
    inserted <- substr(alt, 2, nchar(alt))
    tibble(type = "insertion", rc_pos = pos, rc_end = pos,
           annovar_ref = "-", annovar_alt = inserted, rc_allele = paste0("+", inserted))
  } else {
    # deletion: starts one base after the anchor
    deleted <- substr(ref, 2, nchar(ref))
    tibble(type = "deletion", rc_pos = pos + 1, rc_end = pos + nchar(deleted),
           annovar_ref = deleted, annovar_alt = "-", rc_allele = paste0("-", deleted))
  }
}
```

## 2.2 CHIP flag

**Definition used in this notebook: a Mutect2 call is CHIP if its VCF position
is within 1 bp of the start of a Vanderbilt CHIP call.** The 1 bp window absorbs the indel offset between
the two conventions. The alleles are not compared, so the flag marks CHIP *positions*.

`variant_defs` has one row per distinct variant that Mutect2 called in any sample.

```{r chip-flag}
chip_pos_key <- paste(chip_calls_long$Chr, chip_calls_long$Start)
at_chip_pos  <- function(chrom, pos) paste(chrom, pos) %in% chip_pos_key
chip_gene_at <- function(chrom, pos) chip_calls_long$Gene[match(paste(chrom, pos), chip_pos_key)]

variant_defs <- merged_vcf %>%
  distinct(CHROM, POS, REF, ALT) %>%
  mutate(variant = paste(CHROM, POS, REF, ALT, sep = "_"),
         locus   = pmap(list(POS, REF, ALT), get_variant_locus)) %>%
  unnest(locus) %>%
  mutate(CHIP = as.integer(at_chip_pos(CHROM, POS) | at_chip_pos(CHROM, POS + 1) | at_chip_pos(CHROM, POS - 1)),
         Gene = coalesce(chip_gene_at(CHROM, POS), chip_gene_at(CHROM, POS + 1), chip_gene_at(CHROM, POS - 1)),
         CHIP_lab = factor(ifelse(CHIP == 1, "CHIP", "non-CHIP"), levels = names(chip_colors))) %>%
  # stricter check, for information: the exact Vanderbilt variant (position and alleles)
  left_join(chip_calls_long %>% transmute(CHROM = Chr, rc_pos = Start, annovar_ref = Ref, annovar_alt = Alt, CHIP_exact = 1L),
            by = c("CHROM", "rc_pos", "annovar_ref", "annovar_alt")) %>%
  mutate(CHIP_exact = replace_na(CHIP_exact, 0L))

# two VCF variants never map to the same bam-readcount allele
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(variant_defs[c("CHROM", "rc_pos", "rc_allele")]))

merged_vcf <- merged_vcf %>%
  left_join(variant_defs %>% select(CHROM, POS, REF, ALT, variant, type, CHIP, CHIP_lab, Gene),
            by = c("CHROM", "POS", "REF", "ALT")) %>%
  mutate(traj_id = paste(ID, variant, sep = "_"))

merged_vcf %>%
  group_by(CHIP_lab) %>%
  summarise(calls = n(),
            `PASS calls` = sum(FILTER == "PASS"),
            variants = n_distinct(variant),
            trajectories = n_distinct(traj_id),
            individuals = n_distinct(ID)) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

Variant types:

```{r variant-types}
table(type = variant_defs$type, variant_defs$CHIP_lab)
```

The position rule and the exact Vanderbilt variant disagree for a few variants. They sit at a CHIP position
but carry another allele, and are kept as CHIP here:

```{r chip-position-vs-exact}
table(CHIP_position_rule = variant_defs$CHIP, exact_Vanderbilt_variant = variant_defs$CHIP_exact)

variant_defs %>%
  filter(CHIP == 1, CHIP_exact == 0) %>%
  left_join(merged_vcf %>%
              group_by(variant) %>%
              summarise(calls = n(), individuals = n_distinct(ID), median_AF = median(AF),
                        FILTER = paste(unique(FILTER), collapse = " | ")),
            by = "variant") %>%
  select(variant, Gene, type, calls, individuals, median_AF, FILTER) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

Individuals without any CHIP call. They are left
out of the per-individual trajectory plots below.

```{r ids-no-chip}
ids_no_chip <- setdiff(long_ids, merged_vcf$ID[merged_vcf$CHIP == 1])
ids_no_chip
```

Non-CHIP variants are often shared between individuals. Number of individuals in which each non-CHIP
variant is called:

```{r nonchip-recurrence, fig.height=3.5}
nonchip_recurrence <- merged_vcf %>%
  filter(CHIP == 0) %>%
  group_by(variant, type) %>%
  summarise(N_IDs = n_distinct(ID), calls = n(), `PASS calls` = sum(FILTER == "PASS"), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(-N_IDs)

head(nonchip_recurrence, 10) %>% knitr::kable()

ggplot(nonchip_recurrence, aes(x = N_IDs, fill = type)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, boundary = 0.5) +
  labs(x = paste0("Individuals with a call (of ", length(long_ids), ")"), y = "Non-CHIP variants", fill = NULL)
```


## 2.3 Region lists for bam-readcount

bam-readcount was run at the positions of all CHIP and all non-CHIP variants. The lists on disk
(`resources/chip_vars_for_bam_readcount.txt`, `resources/nonchip_vars_for_bam_readcount.txt`) were written by
an earlier version of this notebook, which placed insertions one base after their anchor position. The pileup therefore
does not contain most insertions (section 3.2).

The lists below use the corrected insertion position. They are compared with the lists on disk and written
only on request, under new names, so that the lists matching the existing pileup stay as they are.

```{r region-lists}
region_list <- function(variants) {
  variants %>%
    distinct(chrom = CHROM, start = rc_pos, end = rc_end) %>%
    arrange(chrom, start)
}

chip_variants    <- region_list(variant_defs %>% filter(CHIP == 1))
nonchip_variants <- region_list(variant_defs %>% filter(CHIP == 0))

read_regions <- function(file) read.table(file, sep = "\t", col.names = c("chrom", "start", "end"))

compare_regions <- function(new, file) {
  disk <- read_regions(file)
  tibble(file = basename(file),
         `regions on disk` = nrow(disk),
         `regions here` = nrow(new),
         `in both` = nrow(inner_join(new, disk, by = c("chrom", "start", "end"))),
         `only on disk` = nrow(anti_join(disk, new, by = c("chrom", "start", "end"))),
         `only here` = nrow(anti_join(new, disk, by = c("chrom", "start", "end"))))
}

bind_rows(compare_regions(chip_variants, "resources/chip_vars_for_bam_readcount.txt"),
          compare_regions(nonchip_variants, "resources/nonchip_vars_for_bam_readcount.txt")) %>%
  knitr::kable()

if (write_region_files) {
  write.table(chip_variants, "resources/chip_vars_for_bam_readcount_corrected.txt",
              sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)
  write.table(nonchip_variants, "resources/nonchip_vars_for_bam_readcount_corrected.txt",
              sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)
}
```

The regions that differ are the insertions (`r sum(variant_defs$type == "insertion")` variants).


# 3. bam-readcount pileup at the variant positions

## 3.1 Pileup files

One row per sample and position, with the alleles seen at that position packed into `var1..varN` as
`allele:count:avg_mapq:avg_baseq`. Regions of neighbouring variants overlap, which lists some positions
more than once per sample; these rows are exact duplicates and are removed.

```{r read-pileup}
read_pileup <- function(file) {
  read.table(file, sep = "\t", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, colClasses = c(ref = "character")) %>%
    distinct()
}

readcount_chip    <- read_pileup("resources/All.chip.bam_readcount.txt")
readcount_nonchip <- read_pileup("resources/All.nonchip.bam_readcount.txt")
```

All sample names of the pileup are in the manifest except two: one sample was piled up twice,
under two suffixed names. The two runs hold the same reads, not two independent measurements: their depths
differ by a few reads per position, far less than two sequencing runs of this depth would (first table).
Adding them up would count every read twice, so one run is used, under the sample name of the manifest. It
is the run whose depth is marginally closer to the Mutect2 records of this sample (second table).

```{r pileup-sample-duplicate}
setdiff(unique(c(readcount_chip$S_ID, readcount_nonchip$S_ID)), samples$Sample)

# the two runs side by side
bind_rows(readcount_chip, readcount_nonchip) %>%
  filter(S_ID %in% c(names(pileup_sample_alias), pileup_sample_drop)) %>%
  distinct(S_ID, chr, pos, depth) %>%
  mutate(run = ifelse(S_ID %in% pileup_sample_drop, "dropped", "used")) %>%
  select(-S_ID) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = run, values_from = depth) %>%
  summarise(positions = n(),
            `depth of the run used, median` = median(used),
            `depth of the run dropped, median` = median(dropped),
            `difference in depth (used - dropped), median` = median(used - dropped),
            `25th to 75th percentile` = paste(quantile(used - dropped, c(0.25, 0.75)), collapse = " to "),
            `positions differing by > 5%` = sum(abs(used - dropped) / used > 0.05),
            `sd of the difference expected for two independent runs` = round(sqrt(2 * median(used)))) %>%
  knitr::kable()

# each run against all Mutect2 SNV records of the sample (before any filter)
mutect_all %>%
  filter(Sample %in% pileup_sample_alias, nchar(REF) == 1, nchar(ALT) == 1) %>%
  inner_join(bind_rows(readcount_chip, readcount_nonchip) %>%
               filter(S_ID %in% c(names(pileup_sample_alias), pileup_sample_drop)) %>%
               distinct(S_ID, chr, pos, depth),
             by = c("CHROM" = "chr", "POS" = "pos"), relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  group_by(run = ifelse(S_ID %in% pileup_sample_drop, "dropped", "used"), S_ID) %>%
  summarise(`Mutect2 SNV records` = n(),
            `Mutect2 DP / pileup depth, median` = round(median(DP / depth), 4),
            `|Mutect2 DP - pileup depth|, mean` = round(mean(abs(DP - depth)), 1),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable()

use_one_run <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    filter(!S_ID %in% pileup_sample_drop) %>%
    mutate(S_ID = coalesce(unname(pileup_sample_alias[S_ID]), S_ID))
}
readcount_chip    <- use_one_run(readcount_chip)
readcount_nonchip <- use_one_run(readcount_nonchip)

stopifnot(all(readcount_chip$S_ID %in% samples$Sample), all(readcount_nonchip$S_ID %in% samples$Sample),
          !anyDuplicated(readcount_chip[c("S_ID", "chr", "pos")]),
          !anyDuplicated(readcount_nonchip[c("S_ID", "chr", "pos")]))
```

```{r pileup-long}

# one row per sample and position (both files), and one row per allele seen there
pileup_sites <- bind_rows(readcount_chip, readcount_nonchip) %>%
  distinct(S_ID, chr, pos, ref, depth)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(pileup_sites[c("S_ID", "chr", "pos")]))

parse_readcount_long <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    select(S_ID, chr, pos, starts_with("var")) %>%
    pivot_longer(starts_with("var"), names_to = NULL, values_to = "allele_str", values_drop_na = TRUE) %>%
    separate(allele_str, into = c("allele", "count"), sep = ":", extra = "drop") %>%
    mutate(count = as.integer(count))
}

pileup_alleles <- bind_rows(parse_readcount_long(readcount_chip), parse_readcount_long(readcount_nonchip)) %>%
  distinct()
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(pileup_alleles[c("S_ID", "chr", "pos", "allele")]))
```

The pileup covers more samples than the Mutect2 calls: all timepoints of the longitudinal individuals and
one sample of each individual of the cross-sectional run.

```{r pileup-samples}
pileup_samples <- tibble(S_ID = unique(pileup_sites$S_ID)) %>%
  left_join(samples, by = c("S_ID" = "Sample"))

pileup_samples %>%
  mutate(group = ifelse(ID %in% long_ids, "longitudinal individual", "individual with a single sample (no VCF here)")) %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(samples = n(), `with Mutect2 VCF` = sum(has_vcf), individuals = n_distinct(ID)) %>%
  knitr::kable()

# every sample with a Mutect2 VCF has a pileup
stopifnot(all(samples$Sample[samples$has_vcf] %in% pileup_samples$S_ID))
```


## 3.2 One row per sample and variant

bam-readcount only reports pileups, it does not know which allele is "the" variant. `readcount_all` crosses
every pileup sample with every variant in `variant_defs` whose locus was queried, and picks the count of
that variant's allele (0 if the allele was not seen). `Detected` marks the samples in which Mutect2 called
the variant.

```{r variant-table}
mutect_calls <- merged_vcf %>%
  distinct(Sample, variant) %>%
  mutate(Detected = 1)

readcount_all <- pileup_sites %>%
  inner_join(samples, by = c("S_ID" = "Sample")) %>%
  inner_join(variant_defs %>% filter(type != "MNV"),
             by = c("chr" = "CHROM", "pos" = "rc_pos"), relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  left_join(pileup_alleles %>% rename(ref_count = count), by = c("S_ID", "chr", "pos", "ref" = "allele")) %>%
  left_join(pileup_alleles %>% rename(alt_count = count), by = c("S_ID", "chr", "pos", "rc_allele" = "allele")) %>%
  left_join(mutect_calls, by = c("S_ID" = "Sample", "variant")) %>%
  mutate(ref_count    = replace_na(ref_count, 0L),
         alt_count    = replace_na(alt_count, 0L),
         Detected     = replace_na(Detected, 0),
         VAF          = alt_count / depth,
         longitudinal = ID %in% long_ids,
         traj_id      = paste(ID, variant, sep = "_")) %>%
  # `alt` is the bam-readcount allele ("C", "-T", "+AT"), not the VCF ALT
  select(ID, S_ID, LABDATE, Age, has_vcf, longitudinal, chr, pos, ref, alt = rc_allele, variant, traj_id,
         type, CHIP, CHIP_lab, Gene, depth, ref_count, alt_count, VAF, Detected)

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(readcount_all[c("S_ID", "variant")]))
```

Variants that can be followed in the pileup. Multi-nucleotide variants have no single pileup allele, and
most insertions were not queried at their own position (section 2.3):

```{r pileup-coverage}
variant_defs %>%
  mutate(`locus in pileup` = variant %in% readcount_all$variant,
         `allele seen in >= 1 sample` = variant %in% readcount_all$variant[readcount_all$alt_count > 0]) %>%
  group_by(CHIP_lab, type) %>%
  summarise(variants = n(), `locus in pileup` = sum(`locus in pileup`),
            `allele seen in >= 1 sample` = sum(`allele seen in >= 1 sample`), .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

Two tables hold the rows with at least one read of the variant allele:

```{r long-tables}
readcount_chip_long    <- readcount_all %>% filter(CHIP == 1, alt_count > 0)
readcount_nonchip_long <- readcount_all %>% filter(CHIP == 0, alt_count > 0)

c(readcount_chip_long = nrow(readcount_chip_long), readcount_nonchip_long = nrow(readcount_nonchip_long))
```


## 3.3 Samples with foreign DNA

At a site where an individual is homozygous for the variant allele, every read should carry it. The share
of reads that do not is a simple measure of DNA from another person in a sample. Homozygous sites are the
non-CHIP SNVs with a median pileup VAF above 0.95 over the timepoints of the individual.

```{r sample-qc, fig.height=4}
sample_qc <- readcount_all %>%
  filter(CHIP == 0, longitudinal, type == "SNV", depth > 0) %>%
  group_by(traj_id) %>%
  filter(median(VAF) > 0.95) %>%
  group_by(ID, S_ID, LABDATE) %>%
  summarise(hom_sites = n(), foreign_read_share = mean(1 - VAF), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(merged_vcf %>% count(Sample, name = "mutect_calls"), by = c("S_ID" = "Sample")) %>%
  left_join(merged_vcf %>% filter(grepl("contamination", FILTER)) %>% count(Sample, name = "calls_flagged_contamination"),
            by = c("S_ID" = "Sample")) %>%
  mutate(mixed = foreign_read_share > mixed_sample_min) %>%
  arrange(-foreign_read_share)

mixed_samples <- sample_qc$S_ID[sample_qc$mixed]

ggplot(sample_qc, aes(x = rank(-foreign_read_share), y = foreign_read_share, colour = mixed)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mixed_sample_min, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(size = 1) +
  geom_text(data = sample_qc %>% filter(mixed), aes(label = paste0(S_ID, " (ID ", ID, ")")), hjust = -0.08, size = 3) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = percent) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "grey40", "TRUE" = "red3"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Samples of longitudinal individuals, ranked", y = "Reads without the individual's\nhomozygous allele (mean over sites)")

head(sample_qc, 6) %>%
  mutate(foreign_read_share = percent(foreign_read_share, accuracy = 0.01)) %>%
  knitr::kable()

# all samples, with the flag and the threshold it was set with
if (write_sample_qc) {
  write.table(sample_qc %>% mutate(mixed_sample_min = mixed_sample_min),
              "resources/SHCS_sample_contamination_QC.txt", sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)
}
```

`r length(mixed_samples)` samples are above `r percent(mixed_sample_min)` (dashed line), against a median of
`r percent(median(sample_qc$foreign_read_share), accuracy = 0.01)`. Foreign DNA adds the other person's germline
variants as low-VAF calls at a single timepoint, which is what non-CHIP variants look like. All samples are
kept in sections 4.1 to 6. The flagged samples are left out of the
final classification (section 4.2) and of the limit of detection (section 7).


# 4. Splitting non-CHIP variants into potential germline and potential somatic

Mutect2's own `germline` flag has already removed most germline variants (section 1.1). What is left is
split per trajectory.

## 4.1 Rule on the Mutect2 AF

A non-CHIP trajectory is **potential germline** if all of its calls have an AF between
`r het_af_range[1]` and `r het_af_range[2]` (heterozygous), or if any call has an AF above `r hom_af_min`
(homozygous). All other trajectories are **potential somatic**. This rule uses all samples and is the one
behind the plots of sections 5 and 6.

```{r split-mutect}
# class of each trajectory from the AF of its Mutect2 calls
mutect_rule <- function(calls) {
  calls %>%
    group_by(ID, variant, traj_id) %>%
    summarise(n_calls  = n(),
              min_AF   = min(AF),
              max_AF   = max(AF),
              het_like = all(AF > het_af_range[1] & AF < het_af_range[2]),
              hom_like = any(AF > hom_af_min),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(class_mutect = ifelse(het_like | hom_like, "potential germline", "potential somatic"))
}

nonchip_class_mutect <- mutect_rule(merged_vcf %>% filter(CHIP == 0))

merged_vcf <- merged_vcf %>%
  left_join(nonchip_class_mutect %>% select(traj_id, class_mutect), by = "traj_id")

nonchip_class_mutect %>%
  group_by(class_mutect) %>%
  summarise(trajectories = n(),
            `with > 1 call` = sum(n_calls > 1),
            calls = sum(n_calls),
            `homozygous-like` = sum(hom_like),
            `heterozygous-like` = sum(het_like & !hom_like)) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r split-mutect-plot, fig.height=3.5}
merged_vcf %>%
  filter(CHIP == 0) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = AF, fill = class_mutect)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.01, boundary = 0) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(het_af_range, hom_af_min), linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = low_af_max, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = pseudo_log_trans(base = 10), breaks = c(0, 10, 100, 1000)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = class_colors) +
  labs(x = "Mutect2 AF of non-CHIP calls", y = "Calls", fill = NULL)
```

Dotted lines: thresholds of the rule. Dashed line: AF `r low_af_max`, the limit
applied to single calls in two plots (section 6.1); no call below it belongs to a potential germline
trajectory.


## 4.2 Check against the pileup and final class

The rule above sees a variant only in the samples where Mutect2 kept it. A germline variant that Mutect2
flags as `germline` at all timepoints but one stays in the table with a single call, and a homozygous
variant in a mixed sample is called well below an AF of `r hom_af_min`. The pileup has the VAF at every
timepoint, so a germline variant shows as a median VAF near 0.5 or 1.

**Final class, used in section 7:** a non-CHIP trajectory is *potential germline* if the rule of 4.1 says so
or if its median pileup VAF over the timepoints of the individual is at least `r low_af_max`; otherwise it
is *potential somatic*. Samples with foreign DNA (section 3.3) are left out of both parts. Trajectories that
Mutect2 never called in the individual are classified by the pileup alone.

```{r split-final}
traj_class <- full_join(
  mutect_rule(merged_vcf %>% filter(CHIP == 0, !Sample %in% mixed_samples)),
  readcount_all %>%
    filter(CHIP == 0, longitudinal, !S_ID %in% mixed_samples, depth > 0) %>%
    group_by(ID, variant, traj_id) %>%
    summarise(pileup_timepoints = n(), pileup_median_VAF = median(VAF), .groups = "drop"),
  by = c("ID", "variant", "traj_id")) %>%
  mutate(mutect_called   = !is.na(class_mutect),
         germline_pileup = pileup_median_VAF >= low_af_max,
         class = ifelse(coalesce(class_mutect == "potential germline", FALSE) | coalesce(germline_pileup, FALSE),
                        "potential germline", "potential somatic"))

traj_class %>%
  filter(mutect_called) %>%
  mutate(pileup = case_when(is.na(germline_pileup) ~ "not in pileup",
                            germline_pileup        ~ paste("median pileup VAF >=", low_af_max),
                            TRUE                   ~ paste("median pileup VAF <", low_af_max))) %>%
  count(`rule of 4.1` = class_mutect, pileup) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = pileup, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Trajectories with a Mutect2 call, samples with foreign DNA left out")
```

The trajectories that are potential germline by the rule of 4.1 but have a low pileup VAF belong to indels
that the pileup does not capture (section 5.1); they keep the class of 4.1.

```{r split-final-plot, fig.height=3.5}
traj_class %>%
  filter(mutect_called, !is.na(pileup_median_VAF)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = pileup_median_VAF, fill = class_mutect)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.02, boundary = 0) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = low_af_max, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = pseudo_log_trans(base = 10), breaks = c(0, 10, 100, 1000)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = class_colors) +
  labs(x = "Median pileup VAF of the trajectory", y = "Trajectories with a Mutect2 call", fill = "Rule of 4.1")
```

```{r split-final-table}
traj_class %>%
  count(`Mutect2 call in the individual` = ifelse(mutect_called, "yes", "no"), class) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = class, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Final class of all non-CHIP trajectories")
```


# 5. Comparing Mutect2 with bam-readcount

## 5.1 Agreement of VAF and depth

Calls that are present in both tables, matched on sample and exact variant.

```{r mutect-vs-pileup}
mutect_vs_pileup <- merged_vcf %>%
  inner_join(readcount_all %>% select(S_ID, variant, depth, pileup_alt = alt_count, VAF_readcount = VAF),
             by = c("Sample" = "S_ID", "variant"))

mutect_vs_pileup %>%
  group_by(CHIP_lab) %>%
  summarise(`Mutect2 calls` = n(),
            `allele seen in pileup` = n_pct(pileup_alt > 0),
            `Spearman rho, AF vs pileup VAF` = round(cor(AF, VAF_readcount, method = "spearman"), 3),
            `|AF - pileup VAF| > 0.02` = sum(abs(AF - VAF_readcount) > 0.02),
            `Mutect2 DP / pileup depth, median` = round(median(DP / depth), 3)) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r mutect-vs-pileup-plot, fig.width=11, fig.height=5}
p_chip <- mutect_vs_pileup %>%
  filter(CHIP == 1) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = AF, y = VAF_readcount, group = traj_id)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Mutect2 AF", y = "bam-readcount VAF", title = "CHIP")

p_nonchip <- mutect_vs_pileup %>%
  filter(CHIP == 0) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = AF, y = VAF_readcount, colour = type)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(size = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(x = "Mutect2 AF", y = "bam-readcount VAF", colour = NULL, title = "non-CHIP")

ggarrange(p_chip, p_nonchip, ncol = 2, widths = c(1, 1.2))

cor.test(~ AF + VAF_readcount, data = mutect_vs_pileup %>% filter(CHIP == 1), method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
```

CHIP calls where the two differ by more than 0.02:

```{r mutect-vs-pileup-discordant}
mutect_vs_pileup %>%
  filter(CHIP == 1, abs(AF - VAF_readcount) > 0.02) %>%
  select(ID, Sample, variant, Gene, FILTER, AF, DP, alt_count, depth, pileup_alt, VAF_readcount) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

For the CHIP variants the two agree. Among the non-CHIP variants there are deletions with a Mutect2 AF of
0.1 to 0.5 and almost no reads in the pileup, and SNVs with more reads in the pileup than in Mutect2.
Mutect2 counts reads after local reassembly, the pileup counts the alleles as they are aligned, so the two
can describe the same event differently, mostly where several variants lie close together (last table of
this section).

Agreement per variant: variant reads in the pileup divided by Mutect2's alternate reads, summed over the
samples where Mutect2 called the variant. Variants with a ratio outside `r pileup_ratio_range[1]` to
`r pileup_ratio_range[2]` (dashed lines) are not followed in the pileup in section 7.

```{r pileup-concordance, fig.height=3.5}
pileup_concordance <- mutect_vs_pileup %>%
  group_by(CHIP_lab, variant, type) %>%
  summarise(calls = n(),
            individuals = n_distinct(ID),
            mutect_alt_reads = sum(alt_count),
            pileup_alt_reads = sum(pileup_alt),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(read_ratio = pileup_alt_reads / mutect_alt_reads,
         pileup_ok  = read_ratio >= pileup_ratio_range[1] & read_ratio <= pileup_ratio_range[2])

pileup_ok_variants <- pileup_concordance$variant[pileup_concordance$pileup_ok]

# ratios below 0.02 (including 0) are drawn at 0.02
ggplot(pileup_concordance, aes(x = pmax(read_ratio, 0.02), fill = type)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 45) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = pileup_ratio_range, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.02, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 10), labels = c("<= 0.02", "0.1", "0.5", "1", "2", "10")) +
  facet_wrap(~CHIP_lab, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Variant reads in the pileup / in Mutect2", y = "Variants", fill = NULL)

pileup_concordance %>%
  group_by(CHIP_lab, type) %>%
  summarise(variants = n(),
            `ratio, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(read_ratio, 2),
            `ratio in range` = sum(pileup_ok),
            `ratio out of range` = sum(!pileup_ok),
            `calls of the variants out of range` = sum(calls[!pileup_ok]),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable()

# Mutect2 flags for variants in a cluster of variants, by agreement with the pileup
pileup_concordance %>%
  filter(CHIP_lab == "non-CHIP") %>%
  left_join(merged_vcf %>%
              group_by(variant) %>%
              summarise(cluster_flag = any(grepl("clustered_events|haplotype", FILTER))),
            by = "variant") %>%
  group_by(`read ratio` = ifelse(pileup_ok, "in range", "out of range")) %>%
  summarise(`non-CHIP variants` = n(),
            `with a clustered_events or haplotype flag` = n_pct(cluster_flag)) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```


## 5.2 Read support of detected and not detected variants

Every variant was queried in all samples, not only where Mutect2 called it. Comparing the reads of the
variant allele between samples with (`Detected = 1`) and without a Mutect2 call shows what separates a call
from the background. Only samples with a Mutect2 VCF are used, and samples without a read of the allele are
included (count 0).

```{r detected-vs-not}
readcount_variants <- readcount_all %>%
  filter(has_vcf, depth > 0) %>%
  mutate(CHIP_lab2    = factor(ifelse(CHIP == 1, "CHIP positions", "Non-CHIP positions"),
                               levels = c("CHIP positions", "Non-CHIP positions")),
         Detected_lab = factor(ifelse(Detected == 1, "Detected", "Not detected"),
                               levels = c("Not detected", "Detected")))

summary_tbl <- readcount_variants %>%
  group_by(CHIP, Detected) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            n_with_alt_reads = sum(alt_count > 0),
            mean_depth = mean(depth),
            mean_alt_count = mean(alt_count), median_alt_count = median(alt_count),
            q25_alt_count = quantile(alt_count, .25), q75_alt_count = quantile(alt_count, .75),
            mean_VAF = mean(VAF), median_VAF = median(VAF),
            .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(summary_tbl, digits = 4)
```

```{r detected-vs-not-tests}
# CHIP positions, detected vs not detected (alt_count)
wilcox.test(alt_count ~ Detected, data = readcount_variants %>% filter(CHIP == 1))
t.test(alt_count ~ Detected, data = readcount_variants %>% filter(CHIP == 1))

# Non-CHIP positions, detected vs not detected (alt_count)
wilcox.test(alt_count ~ Detected, data = readcount_variants %>% filter(CHIP == 0))
t.test(alt_count ~ Detected, data = readcount_variants %>% filter(CHIP == 0))
```

```{r detected-vs-not-plots, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
col_detected    <- "#2a78d6"
col_notdetected <- "#898781"

ggplot(readcount_variants, aes(x = Detected_lab, y = alt_count + 1, fill = Detected_lab)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.15, width = 0.55, linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Not detected" = col_notdetected, "Detected" = col_detected), guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~CHIP_lab2) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Alt allele read count (+1, log10 scale)",
       title = "Read support for CHIP vs non-CHIP variants, by Mutect2 detection status") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#f0efec", color = NA),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#e1e0d9", linewidth = 0.3))

ggplot(readcount_variants, aes(x = Detected_lab, y = VAF, fill = Detected_lab)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.15, width = 0.55, linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 0.6)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Not detected" = col_notdetected, "Detected" = col_detected), guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~CHIP_lab2) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Variant allele fraction (alt_count / depth)",
       title = "VAF for CHIP vs non-CHIP variants, by Mutect2 detection status") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#f0efec", color = NA),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#e1e0d9", linewidth = 0.3))
```

The high-VAF tail among the non-CHIP "not detected" observations is germline: variants that Mutect2 flagged
as `germline` or `multiallelic` in that sample, which removed them from `merged_vcf` (section 1.1) although
the reads are there.

```{r not-detected-high-vaf}
readcount_variants %>%
  filter(CHIP == 0, Detected == 0) %>%
  count(`pileup VAF` = cut(VAF, c(0, 1e-9, 0.02, low_af_max, 1), include.lowest = TRUE,
                           labels = c("0", "> 0 to 0.02", paste("0.02 to", low_af_max), paste(">", low_af_max))),
        name = "not detected observations") %>%
  knitr::kable()
```


## 5.3 CHIP variants in the pileup, by detection status

The pileup follows a CHIP clone at the timepoints where Mutect2 did not call it. Example individual SHCS_3:
all CHIP alleles with at least one read (including alleles of other individuals' clones, which stay near
zero), then only the variants that Mutect2 called at least once in this individual, then the read count
against depth. Point shape: Mutect2 call in that sample.

```{r chip-pileup-example, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
detected_shape <- scale_shape_manual(values = c("0" = 16, "1" = 17), labels = c("0" = "no", "1" = "yes"),
                                     name = "Mutect2 call", na.translate = FALSE)

chip_example <- readcount_chip_long %>% filter(ID == id_of("SHCS_3"))

ggplot(chip_example, aes(x = Age, y = VAF, group = traj_id, shape = as.factor(Detected))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = chip_vaf, linetype = "dashed") +
  detected_shape

chip_example %>%
  group_by(traj_id) %>%
  filter(sum(Detected) > 0) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Age, y = VAF, group = traj_id, shape = as.factor(Detected))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = chip_vaf, linetype = "dashed") +
  detected_shape

ggplot(chip_example, aes(x = depth, y = alt_count, group = traj_id, shape = as.factor(Detected))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  detected_shape
```

The same for all longitudinal individuals:

```{r chip-pileup-all, fig.width=14, fig.height=11}
chip_long_ids <- readcount_chip_long %>% filter(longitudinal)

ggplot(chip_long_ids, aes(x = Age, y = VAF, group = traj_id, shape = as.factor(Detected))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = chip_vaf, linetype = "dashed") +
  detected_shape +
  facet_wrap(~ID)

chip_long_ids %>%
  group_by(traj_id) %>%
  filter(sum(Detected) > 0) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Age, y = VAF, group = traj_id, shape = as.factor(Detected))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = chip_vaf, linetype = "dashed") +
  detected_shape +
  facet_wrap(~ID)

ggplot(chip_long_ids, aes(x = depth, y = alt_count, group = traj_id, shape = as.factor(Detected))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  detected_shape +
  facet_wrap(~ID)
```

```{r chip-pileup-depth, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
p_all <- ggplot(chip_long_ids, aes(x = depth, y = alt_count, group = traj_id, shape = as.factor(Detected))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  detected_shape

p_depth <- ggplot(chip_long_ids, aes(y = depth, x = as.factor(Detected))) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("0" = "no", "1" = "yes")) +
  labs(x = "Mutect2 call")

ggarrange(p_all, p_depth, ncol = 2, widths = c(1.6, 1), common.legend = TRUE, legend = "right")
```


# 6. Exploring non-CHIP variants and comparing them with CHIP variants

## 6.1 Mutect2 calls

### Trajectories per individual

Trajectories with more than one call. Non-CHIP trajectories are the potential somatic ones (rule of 4.1).
Dashed line: VAF `r chip_vaf`.

```{r mutect-trajectories, fig.width=14, fig.height=12}
# trajectories with more than one Mutect2 call, in individuals with CHIP
multi_call <- merged_vcf %>%
  group_by(traj_id) %>%
  filter(n() > 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!ID %in% ids_no_chip)

chip_multi    <- multi_call %>% filter(CHIP == 1)
nonchip_multi <- multi_call %>% filter(CHIP == 0, class_mutect == "potential somatic")

c(CHIP_trajectories = n_distinct(chip_multi$traj_id), non_CHIP_trajectories = n_distinct(nonchip_multi$traj_id))

bind_rows(chip_multi, nonchip_multi) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = LABDATE, y = AF, group = traj_id, colour = CHIP_lab)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = chip_vaf, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = chip_colors) +
  labs(colour = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~ID, scales = "free")
```

### AF of non-CHIP calls

All non-CHIP calls with an AF below `r low_af_max`, over time and as a distribution.

```{r nonchip-af, fig.height=4.5}
nonchip_low <- merged_vcf %>%
  filter(CHIP == 0, AF < low_af_max)

ggplot(nonchip_low, aes(x = LABDATE, y = AF, group = traj_id)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.6, color = "grey") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = chip_vaf, linetype = "dashed")

ggplot(nonchip_low, aes(y = AF)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = chip_vaf, linetype = "dashed") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 0.05))

summary(nonchip_low$AF)
```

Per individual:

```{r nonchip-af-per-id, fig.width=14, fig.height=11}
ggplot(nonchip_low, aes(y = AF)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = chip_vaf, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ID, scales = "free")

nonchip_low %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  summarise(calls = n(), min_AF = min(AF), lowQ_AF = quantile(AF, 0.25), median_AF = median(AF),
            highQ_AF = quantile(AF, 0.75), max_AF = max(AF))
```

### AF against depth

A clone has the same expected AF at any depth. An AF that falls as depth rises is expected for calls at the
detection limit (the lowest AF that can be called falls with depth) and for artefacts whose number of reads
does not scale with depth. Lines join the calls of one trajectory; blue: fit over all calls.

Non-CHIP (potential somatic trajectories with more than one call):

```{r af-vs-depth-nonchip, fig.height=4.5}
ggplot(nonchip_multi, aes(x = DP, y = AF, group = traj_id)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_smooth(group = 1)

ggplot(nonchip_multi, aes(x = DP, y = AF, group = traj_id)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_smooth(group = 1, method = "lm") +
  scale_y_log10()

ggplot(nonchip_multi, aes(x = DP, y = AF, group = traj_id)) +
  geom_smooth(colour = "grey", se = FALSE, method = "lm", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(group = 1, method = "lm") +
  scale_y_log10()
```

CHIP:

```{r af-vs-depth-chip, fig.height=4.5}
ggplot(chip_multi, aes(x = DP, y = AF, group = traj_id)) +
  geom_line(colour = "grey", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(group = 1, method = "lm") +
  scale_y_log10()

ggplot(chip_multi, aes(x = DP, y = AF, group = traj_id)) +
  geom_smooth(colour = "grey", se = FALSE, method = "lm", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(group = 1, method = "lm") +
  scale_y_log10()
```

The two fits as numbers. The slope is that of `log10(AF) ~ DP` over all calls, per 1000 reads of depth;
calls of one trajectory are not independent, so the interval is too narrow.

```{r af-vs-depth-table}
bind_rows(chip_multi, nonchip_multi) %>%
  group_by(CHIP_lab) %>%
  summarise(trajectories = n_distinct(traj_id),
            calls = n(),
            `Spearman rho, AF vs DP` = round(cor(AF, DP, method = "spearman"), 3),
            fit = list(broom::tidy(lm(log10(AF) ~ I(DP / 1000)), conf.int = TRUE)[2, ]),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  unnest(fit) %>%
  transmute(CHIP_lab, trajectories, calls, `Spearman rho, AF vs DP`,
            `slope of log10(AF) per 1000 reads (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.3f (%.3f to %.3f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high)) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```


## 6.2 Pileup

### Depth at CHIP and non-CHIP positions

All positions of the two pileup files, all samples.

```{r depth-chip-vs-nonchip, fig.width=5, fig.height=4}
df <- bind_rows(readcount_chip    %>% select(S_ID, chr, pos, ref, depth) %>% mutate(CHIP = 1),
                readcount_nonchip %>% select(S_ID, chr, pos, ref, depth) %>% mutate(CHIP = 0))

ggplot(df, aes(y = depth, x = as.factor(CHIP))) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("0" = "non-CHIP positions", "1" = "CHIP positions")) +
  labs(x = NULL)

t.test(df$depth ~ df$CHIP)
wilcox.test(df$depth ~ df$CHIP)
```

### Non-CHIP alleles over time

Every non-CHIP allele with at least one read, in the longitudinal individuals. The bands near 0.5 and 1 are
germline variants; most of them are not in `merged_vcf` for that individual because Mutect2 flagged them.

```{r nonchip-pileup-all, fig.width=14, fig.height=11}
nonchip_long_ids <- readcount_nonchip_long %>% filter(longitudinal)

ggplot(nonchip_long_ids, aes(x = Age, y = VAF, group = traj_id)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = chip_vaf, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ID)
```

Individual SHCS_34. At one timepoint the germline variants leave their bands (homozygous variants drop,
absent alleles appear): this is the
sample with the largest share of foreign DNA in section 3.3.

```{r nonchip-pileup-example-mixed, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
nonchip_long_ids %>%
  filter(ID == id_of("SHCS_34")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Age, y = VAF, group = traj_id)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = chip_vaf, linetype = "dashed")
```

Individual SHCS_1, trajectories with a mean VAF below `r chip_vaf`:

```{r nonchip-pileup-example-low-vaf, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
nonchip_long_ids %>%
  filter(ID == id_of("SHCS_1")) %>%
  group_by(traj_id) %>%
  filter(mean(VAF) < chip_vaf) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Age, y = VAF, group = traj_id)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = chip_vaf, linetype = "dashed")
```

### Mean VAF of the low-VAF trajectories

One row per trajectory with at least one read of the allele. `mean_VAF` and the other statistics are taken
over the timepoints where the allele was seen. The density of all individuals in the pileup includes
the individuals with a single sample; the density of the longitudinal individuals is shown next to it.

```{r nonchip-mean-vaf, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
Mode <- function(x) {
  ux <- unique(x)
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}

# statistics over the timepoints with >= 1 read of the allele; timepoints without a read count as missed
nonchip_traj <- readcount_all %>%
  filter(CHIP == 0) %>%
  group_by(ID, longitudinal, traj_id) %>%
  summarise(n_timepoints_total    = n(),
            n_timepoints_detected = sum(alt_count > 0),
            mean_VAF   = mean(VAF[alt_count > 0]),
            median_VAF = median(VAF[alt_count > 0]),
            min_VAF    = min(VAF[alt_count > 0]),
            max_VAF    = max(VAF[alt_count > 0]),
            mode_VAF   = Mode(VAF[alt_count > 0]),
            sd_VAF     = sd(VAF[alt_count > 0]),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_timepoints_detected > 0) %>%
  mutate(CV_VAF = sd_VAF / mean_VAF,
         n_timepoints_missed = n_timepoints_total - n_timepoints_detected,
         frac_missed = n_timepoints_missed / n_timepoints_total)

readcount_nonchip_long_sum <- nonchip_traj %>% filter(mean_VAF <= chip_vaf)

bind_rows(readcount_nonchip_long_sum %>% mutate(set = "all individuals in the pileup (original)"),
          readcount_nonchip_long_sum %>% filter(longitudinal) %>% mutate(set = "longitudinal individuals")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_VAF, colour = set)) +
  geom_density() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("black", "red3")) +
  labs(colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

readcount_nonchip_long_sum %>%
  select(mean_VAF, median_VAF, min_VAF, max_VAF, mode_VAF) %>%
  summary()

# most frequent value of mean_VAF, and the peak of its density
dens <- density(readcount_nonchip_long_sum$mean_VAF)
c(Mode = Mode(readcount_nonchip_long_sum$mean_VAF), density_peak = dens$x[which.max(dens$y)])
```

### How often is a low-VAF trajectory missed at a timepoint?

A timepoint is *missed* when the pileup has no read of the allele there. Trajectories with a mean VAF below
`r chip_vaf` are split into deciles of mean VAF. Only the longitudinal individuals are used: an individual
with a single sample cannot miss a timepoint.

```{r missed-by-decile}
add_deciles <- function(traj) {
  traj %>%
    filter(mean_VAF < chip_vaf) %>%
    mutate(VAF_decile = ntile(mean_VAF, 10))
}

decile_summary <- function(traj) {
  traj %>%
    group_by(VAF_decile) %>%
    summarise(n_trajectories = n(),
              min_mean_VAF = min(mean_VAF),
              max_mean_VAF = max(mean_VAF),
              pct_never_missed = round(100 * mean(n_timepoints_missed == 0), 1),
              mean_frac_missed = mean(frac_missed),
              median_frac_missed = median(frac_missed),
              .groups = "drop")
}

# deciles x number of missed timepoints, as counts or as % of the decile
missed_crosstab <- function(traj, percent = FALSE) {
  traj %>%
    count(VAF_decile, n_timepoints_missed, name = "n_trajectories") %>%
    group_by(VAF_decile) %>%
    mutate(value = if (percent) round(100 * n_trajectories / sum(n_trajectories), 1) else n_trajectories) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    arrange(n_timepoints_missed) %>%
    select(VAF_decile, n_timepoints_missed, value) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = n_timepoints_missed, values_from = value, names_prefix = "missed_", values_fill = 0) %>%
    arrange(VAF_decile)
}

low_vaf_traj <- add_deciles(nonchip_traj %>% filter(longitudinal))

decile_summary(low_vaf_traj) %>% knitr::kable(digits = 5)
missed_crosstab(low_vaf_traj) %>% knitr::kable(caption = "Trajectories by number of missed timepoints")
missed_crosstab(low_vaf_traj, percent = TRUE) %>% knitr::kable(caption = "% of the trajectories of the decile")
```

```{r missed-by-decile-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
low_vaf_traj %>%
  count(VAF_decile, n_timepoints_missed) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(VAF_decile), y = n, fill = fct_rev(factor(n_timepoints_missed)))) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "YlOrRd", direction = -1) +
  labs(x = "Decile of mean VAF (trajectories with mean VAF < 0.02)", y = "Trajectories", fill = "Timepoints\nmissed")
```

The same for *stable* trajectories: coefficient of variation of the VAF (`CV_VAF = sd_VAF / mean_VAF`) at
or below the median of the low-VAF trajectories. Trajectories seen at a single timepoint have no CV and are
left out.

```{r missed-stable}
cv_threshold <- median(low_vaf_traj$CV_VAF, na.rm = TRUE)
cv_threshold

stable_traj <- low_vaf_traj %>%
  filter(!is.na(CV_VAF), CV_VAF <= cv_threshold)

decile_summary(stable_traj) %>% knitr::kable(digits = 5)
missed_crosstab(stable_traj) %>% knitr::kable(caption = "Stable trajectories by number of missed timepoints")
missed_crosstab(stable_traj, percent = TRUE) %>% knitr::kable(caption = "% of the stable trajectories of the decile")
```

The same on all individuals in the pileup. The individuals with a single sample never
miss a timepoint, which raises the share of trajectories that are never missed (left column: all individuals
in the pileup):

```{r missed-original-set}
bind_rows(decile_summary(add_deciles(nonchip_traj)) %>% mutate(set = "all individuals in the pileup"),
          decile_summary(low_vaf_traj) %>% mutate(set = "longitudinal individuals")) %>%
  transmute(VAF_decile, set, cell = sprintf("%.1f%% of %d", pct_never_missed, n_trajectories)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = set, values_from = cell) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Trajectories never missed, by decile of mean VAF")
```


# 7. Limit of detection of non-CHIP variants (`chip_lod`)

## 7.1 Package and data

For a site with depth `n` and `k` reads of the variant allele, `lod_frequentist()` returns:

| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| `lambda_bg` | `n * e / 3`, expected number of error reads carrying the specific alternate base |
| `pvalue` | P(K >= k) under Poisson(`lambda_bg`), i.e. sequencing error alone |
| `k_star` | smallest read count with `pvalue <= alpha` at this depth |
| `called` | `k >= k_star` |
| `lod_vaf` | smallest true VAF that reaches `k_star` reads with probability >= `power_target` at this depth |

`k_star` and `lod_vaf` depend only on depth. The package is in `external/chip_lod`;
only `model.R` and `lod.R` are sourced, into their own environment.

```{r chip-lod-package}
chip_lod <- new.env()
for (f in c("model.R", "lod.R")) {
  sys.source(file.path("external/chip_lod", "r", "R", f), envir = chip_lod)
}
lod_frequentist <- chip_lod$lod_frequentist

# example from the package README
lod_frequentist(n = c(500, 1000, 2000), k = c(3, 1, 3), e = 0.001)
```

Two tables go into the calculation, both without the samples with foreign DNA (section 3.3):

- **`lod_calls`**: every non-CHIP Mutect2 call, with Mutect2's own counts (`n = DP`, `k` = alternate reads
  of `AD`). This covers all variant types.
- **`lod_obs`**: every non-CHIP SNV and deletion at **every timepoint** of every longitudinal individual,
  with the pileup counts (`k = 0` where the allele was not seen). This is what a trajectory needs.
  Insertions and multi-nucleotide variants are not in the pileup (section 3.2), and variants whose pileup
  counts do not agree with Mutect2 are left out (section 5.1).

```{r lod-data}
lod_calls <- merged_vcf %>%
  filter(CHIP == 0, !Sample %in% mixed_samples) %>%
  left_join(traj_class %>% select(traj_id, class), by = "traj_id") %>%
  transmute(ID, Sample, Age, variant, traj_id, type, FILTER, class, n = DP, k = alt_count)

lod_obs <- readcount_all %>%
  filter(CHIP == 0, longitudinal, !S_ID %in% mixed_samples, depth > 0,
         type %in% c("SNV", "deletion"), variant %in% pileup_ok_variants) %>%
  left_join(traj_class %>% select(traj_id, class, mutect_called), by = "traj_id") %>%
  transmute(ID, Sample = S_ID, LABDATE, Age, variant, traj_id, type, class, mutect_called, has_vcf, Detected,
            n = depth, k = alt_count) %>%
  group_by(ID) %>%
  mutate(timepoint = dense_rank(LABDATE)) %>%
  ungroup()

c(lod_calls = nrow(lod_calls), lod_obs = nrow(lod_obs), lod_obs_trajectories = n_distinct(lod_obs$traj_id),
  samples_in_lod_obs = n_distinct(lod_obs$Sample), individuals = n_distinct(lod_obs$ID))
```

`lod_frequentist()` is run once on the distinct (`n`, `k`) pairs of both tables and joined back. The
bisection in the package takes about 40 ms per distinct depth (2 to 3 minutes for this chunk).

```{r lod-run}
lod_pairs <- bind_rows(lod_calls %>% distinct(n, k), lod_obs %>% distinct(n, k)) %>%
  distinct()

lod_tab <- lod_frequentist(n = lod_pairs$n, k = lod_pairs$k,
                           e = err_rate, alpha = alpha, power_target = power_tgt)
stopifnot(all(lod_tab$n == lod_pairs$n), all(lod_tab$k == lod_pairs$k))

# vaf is the raw read fraction k / n, on the same scale as lod_vaf
add_lod <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    left_join(lod_tab, by = c("n", "k")) %>%
    mutate(vaf = k / n,
           status = case_when(is.na(lod_vaf) ~ NA_character_,
                              !called        ~ "not called (k < k*)",
                              vaf < lod_vaf  ~ "called, VAF < LoD",
                              TRUE           ~ "VAF >= LoD"),
           status = factor(status, levels = status_levels))
}

lod_calls <- add_lod(lod_calls)
lod_obs   <- add_lod(lod_obs)

# at very low depth no VAF up to 0.5 reaches the target power, and the package returns no LoD
c(lod_obs_without_LoD = sum(is.na(lod_obs$lod_vaf)), lod_calls_without_LoD = sum(is.na(lod_calls$lod_vaf)))
lod_obs   <- lod_obs %>% filter(!is.na(lod_vaf))
lod_calls <- lod_calls %>% filter(!is.na(lod_vaf))
```

`status` combines the two package results for each observation:

- **not called (k < k\*)**: the reads are compatible with sequencing error alone.
- **called, VAF < LoD**: more reads than error explains, but a variant of this size would be missed in more
  than `r 100 * (1 - power_tgt)`% of measurements at this depth.
- **VAF >= LoD**: reliably detectable at this depth. This is "above the LoD" below.

Groups of trajectories used below:

```{r lod-groups}
group_levels <- c("Mutect2-called, potential somatic", "Mutect2-called, potential germline",
                  "pileup only, potential somatic", "pileup only, potential germline")

lod_obs <- lod_obs %>%
  mutate(group = factor(paste0(ifelse(mutect_called, "Mutect2-called, ", "pileup only, "), class), levels = group_levels))

lod_obs %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(trajectories = n_distinct(traj_id), variants = n_distinct(variant), individuals = n_distinct(ID),
            observations = n(), `observations with a Mutect2 call` = sum(Detected)) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

*Mutect2-called*: Mutect2 called the variant in at least one sample of the individual. *Pileup only*: the
variant was called in other individuals but never in this one; these trajectories show what the same sites
look like without a call.


## 7.2 Limit of detection of the observations

```{r lod-summary}
lod_obs %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  summarise(observations = n(),
            `depth, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(n),
            `depth, range` = paste(range(n), collapse = "-"),
            `k*, range` = paste(range(k_star), collapse = "-"),
            `LoD VAF %, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(lod_vaf, 2, 100),
            `LoD VAF %, range` = paste(round(100 * range(lod_vaf), 2), collapse = "-"),
            `LoD <= 0.5% VAF` = percent(mean(lod_vaf <= 0.005), accuracy = 0.1),
            `LoD <= 1% VAF` = percent(mean(lod_vaf <= 0.01), accuracy = 0.1),
            `LoD <= 2% VAF` = percent(mean(lod_vaf <= chip_vaf), accuracy = 0.1)) %>%
  knitr::kable()

# all observations together
lod_obs %>%
  summarise(observations = n(),
            `depth, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(n),
            `k* (share of observations)` = paste(sprintf("%d: %.1f%%", as.integer(names(table(k_star))),
                                                        100 * prop.table(table(k_star))), collapse = ", "),
            `LoD VAF %, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(lod_vaf, 2, 100),
            `LoD VAF %, 5th-95th percentile` = paste(round(100 * quantile(lod_vaf, c(0.05, 0.95)), 2), collapse = "-")) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

The LoD is a property of depth, so it is the same for all groups. Every observed depth with its `k_star`
and `lod_vaf`, and the depth distribution of the observations:

```{r lod-curve, fig.height=5.5}
lod_curve <- lod_obs %>%
  distinct(n, k_star, lod_vaf) %>%
  arrange(n)

p_curve <- ggplot(lod_curve, aes(x = n, y = lod_vaf, colour = factor(k_star))) +
  geom_point(size = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = chip_vaf, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_log10(limits = range(lod_curve$n)) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "LoD VAF", colour = "k*")

p_depth <- ggplot(lod_obs, aes(x = n)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 80, fill = "grey60") +
  scale_x_log10(limits = range(lod_curve$n)) +
  labs(x = "Depth at the variant site", y = "Observations")

ggarrange(p_curve, p_depth, ncol = 1, heights = c(1.6, 1), align = "v", legend = "right")
```


## 7.3 How many variants are above the LoD

### Mutect2 calls (Mutect2 read counts)

Every non-CHIP call, all variant types.

```{r lod-calls}
lod_calls %>%
  mutate(filter = ifelse(FILTER == "PASS", "PASS", "other flags")) %>%
  group_by(class, filter) %>%
  summarise(calls = n(),
            `depth, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(n),
            `alt reads, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(k),
            `LoD VAF %, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(lod_vaf, 2, 100),
            `VAF %, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(vaf, 2, 100),
            `called (k >= k*)` = n_pct(called),
            `VAF >= LoD` = n_pct(status == "VAF >= LoD"),
            `lowest VAF / LoD` = round(min(vaf / lod_vaf), 2),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable()

# potential somatic calls by variant type
lod_calls %>%
  filter(class == "potential somatic") %>%
  group_by(type) %>%
  summarise(calls = n(),
            variants = n_distinct(variant),
            `VAF %, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(vaf, 2, 100),
            `called (k >= k*)` = n_pct(called),
            `VAF >= LoD` = n_pct(status == "VAF >= LoD")) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

### All timepoints (pileup read counts)

```{r lod-status-table}
status_table <- function(df, ...) {
  df %>%
    count(..., status) %>%
    group_by(...) %>%
    mutate(cell = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, 100 * n / sum(n)), observations = sum(n)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(-n) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = status, values_from = cell, values_fill = "0", names_sort = TRUE)
}

status_table(lod_obs, group) %>% knitr::kable()
```

Mutect2-called trajectories, split by whether Mutect2 called the variant in that sample. A few timepoints
of the pileup have no Mutect2 VCF (section 3.1) and are shown separately.

```{r lod-status-by-call}
lod_obs <- lod_obs %>%
  mutate(sample_call = case_when(!has_vcf      ~ "no VCF for this sample",
                                 Detected == 1 ~ "Mutect2 call in this sample",
                                 TRUE          ~ "no Mutect2 call in this sample"))

lod_obs %>%
  filter(mutect_called) %>%
  status_table(group, sample_call) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r lod-status-plot, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.5}
lod_obs %>%
  ggplot(aes(y = fct_rev(group), fill = fct_rev(status))) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = status_colors, breaks = status_levels) +
  labs(x = "Observations", y = NULL, fill = NULL)
```

Observed reads against the thresholds. Each point is one observation with at least one read of the allele.
Solid line: `lod_vaf`. Dotted line: `k_star / depth`, the read fraction needed to be called.

```{r lod-vaf-vs-depth, fig.width=12, fig.height=7}
vaf_trans  <- pseudo_log_trans(sigma = 2e-4, base = 10)
vaf_breaks <- c(0, 0.001, 0.005, 0.02, 0.1, 0.5)

lod_obs %>%
  filter(k > 0) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = vaf)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = status), size = 0.5, alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(data = lod_curve, aes(y = lod_vaf, linetype = "LoD VAF")) +
  geom_line(data = lod_curve, aes(y = k_star / n, linetype = "k* / depth")) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = vaf_trans, breaks = vaf_breaks, labels = percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = status_colors) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("LoD VAF" = "solid", "k* / depth" = "dotted")) +
  facet_wrap(~group) +
  labs(x = "Depth", y = "Observed VAF (k / n)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2, alpha = 1))) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## 7.5 Trajectories: do they stay above the LoD?

One row per trajectory, over all timepoints of the individual (timepoints without a read count as VAF 0).

```{r lod-trajectories}
consistency_levels <- c("all timepoints above LoD", "some timepoints above LoD", "no timepoint above LoD")

lod_traj <- lod_obs %>%
  group_by(group, class, mutect_called, ID, variant, traj_id, type) %>%
  summarise(timepoints = n(),
            n_above    = sum(status == "VAF >= LoD"),
            n_called   = sum(called),
            n_mutect   = sum(Detected),
            mean_vaf   = mean(vaf),
            min_vaf    = min(vaf),
            max_vaf    = max(vaf),
            mean_vaf_above = mean(vaf[status == "VAF >= LoD"]),
            mean_lod   = mean(lod_vaf),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(frac_above  = n_above / timepoints,
         consistency = factor(case_when(n_above == timepoints ~ consistency_levels[1],
                                        n_above == 0          ~ consistency_levels[3],
                                        TRUE                  ~ consistency_levels[2]),
                              levels = consistency_levels)) %>%
  # Mutect2 PASS calls of the trajectory, and number of individuals in which the variant is called
  left_join(lod_calls %>% group_by(traj_id) %>% summarise(n_pass = sum(FILTER == "PASS")), by = "traj_id") %>%
  left_join(nonchip_recurrence %>% select(variant, N_IDs), by = "variant") %>%
  mutate(n_pass = replace_na(n_pass, 0L))

table(timepoints_per_trajectory = lod_traj$timepoints)
```

```{r lod-trajectories-table}
lod_traj %>%
  count(group, consistency) %>%
  group_by(group) %>%
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, 100 * n / sum(n)), trajectories = sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-n) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = consistency, values_from = cell, values_fill = "0") %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

Mean VAF of the trajectories. `mean VAF` is the mean over all timepoints of a trajectory; the table gives
the mean and the median of this value over the trajectories of each row.

            variants = n_distinct(variant),

            `mean VAF %, mean over trajectories` = round(100 * mean(mean_vaf), 3),
            `mean VAF %, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(mean_vaf, 3, 100),
            `lowest VAF of the trajectory %, median` = round(100 * median(min_vaf), 3),
            `highest VAF of the trajectory %, median` = round(100 * median(max_vaf), 3),

Potential somatic trajectories with a Mutect2 call, by number of individuals in which the same variant is
called (all samples, section 2.2), and by whether the trajectory has a `PASS` call. A variant called in most
individuals is a property of the site (artefact or polymorphism), not a clone.

```{r lod-trajectories-recurrence}
consistency_summary <- function(traj) {
  traj %>%
    summarise(variants = n_distinct(variant),
              trajectories = n(),
              `all timepoints above LoD` = n_pct(consistency == consistency_levels[1]),
              `some` = n_pct(consistency == consistency_levels[2]),
              `none` = n_pct(consistency == consistency_levels[3]),
              `mean VAF %, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(mean_vaf, 3, 100),
              .groups = "drop")
}

som_traj <- lod_traj %>%
  filter(group == "Mutect2-called, potential somatic") %>%
  mutate(`individuals with a call` = cut(N_IDs, c(0, 1, 5, 20, Inf), labels = c("1", "2-5", "6-20", "> 20")),
         `PASS call in the trajectory` = ifelse(n_pass > 0, "yes", "no"))

som_traj %>% group_by(`individuals with a call`) %>% consistency_summary() %>% knitr::kable()
som_traj %>% group_by(`PASS call in the trajectory`) %>% consistency_summary() %>% knitr::kable()
som_traj %>%
  filter(N_IDs == 1) %>%
  group_by(`individuals with a call`, `PASS call in the trajectory`) %>%
  consistency_summary() %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Variants called in a single individual")
```
