## 7.6 Stringent set: PASS calls of non-recurrent variants

Most of the potential somatic trajectories above carry Mutect2 filter flags or belong to variants that occur
in many individuals. The stringent set keeps a trajectory only if

1. Mutect2 called the variant with `FILTER == "PASS"` in at least one sample of the individual, and
2. the variant is found in at most `r max_individuals` of the `r length(long_ids)` individuals
   (`max_individuals`). "Found" is counted in two ways, and both have to hold: individuals with a Mutect2
   call of the variant under any filter (section 2.2), and individuals in whose pileup the variant is above
   the LoD at one timepoint or more.

The pileup count is needed because Mutect2 can call a variant in one individual although the same reads are
in the pileup of most others.

```{r lod-stringent-set}
# individuals in whose pileup each variant is above the LoD at >= 1 timepoint
pileup_recurrence <- lod_obs %>%
  group_by(variant) %>%
  summarise(ids_above_lod = n_distinct(ID[status == "VAF >= LoD"]), .groups = "drop")

lod_traj <- lod_traj %>%
  left_join(pileup_recurrence, by = "variant") %>%
  mutate(stringent = group == "Mutect2-called, potential somatic" & n_pass > 0 &
                     N_IDs <= max_individuals & ids_above_lod <= max_individuals)

som_all <- lod_traj %>% filter(group == "Mutect2-called, potential somatic")

tibble(step = c("potential somatic trajectories with a Mutect2 call, followed in the pileup",
                "... with a PASS call",
                paste("... and variant called by Mutect2 in <=", max_individuals, "individuals"),
                paste("... and variant above the LoD in the pileup of <=", max_individuals, "individuals: stringent set")),
       keep = list(rep(TRUE, nrow(som_all)),
                   som_all$n_pass > 0,
                   som_all$n_pass > 0 & som_all$N_IDs <= max_individuals,
                   som_all$stringent)) %>%
  mutate(trajectories = map_int(keep, sum),
         variants     = map_int(keep, ~ n_distinct(som_all$variant[.x])),
         individuals  = map_int(keep, ~ n_distinct(som_all$ID[.x]))) %>%
  select(-keep) %>%
  knitr::kable()

stringent_traj <- lod_traj %>% filter(stringent)
stringent_obs  <- lod_obs %>% filter(traj_id %in% stringent_traj$traj_id)

# potential somatic trajectories with a PASS call that are not followed in the pileup
pass_traj_ids <- lod_calls %>% filter(class == "potential somatic", FILTER == "PASS") %>% distinct(traj_id, type)
table(type = pass_traj_ids$type, followed_in_pileup = pass_traj_ids$traj_id %in% lod_traj$traj_id)
```

The second table counts the potential somatic trajectories with a `PASS` call by variant type. Those that
are not followed in the pileup are insertions, multi-nucleotide variants and variants whose pileup counts do
not agree with Mutect2 (sections 3.2 and 5.1); they are not part of the stringent set.

The two counts of recurrence for the variants with a `PASS` call. Dashed lines: `max_individuals`.

```{r lod-stringent-recurrence, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=4.5}
som_all %>%
  filter(n_pass > 0) %>%
  distinct(variant, type, N_IDs, ids_above_lod) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = N_IDs, y = ids_above_lod, colour = type)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = max_individuals + 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = max_individuals + 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.25, height = 0.25, size = 1.3, alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(x = "Individuals with a Mutect2 call of the variant (any filter)",
       y = "Individuals with the variant above the LoD\nin the pileup (>= 1 timepoint)", colour = NULL)
```

### Observations

```{r lod-stringent-status}
bind_rows(stringent_obs %>% mutate(sample_call = "all timepoints"), stringent_obs) %>%
  mutate(sample_call = fct_relevel(sample_call, "all timepoints")) %>%
  status_table(sample_call) %>%
  knitr::kable()

stringent_obs %>%
  group_by(status) %>%
  summarise(observations = n(),
            `alt reads, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(k),
            `VAF %, mean` = round(100 * mean(vaf), 3),
            `VAF %, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(vaf, 3, 100),
            `VAF %, range` = paste(round(100 * range(vaf), 3), collapse = "-"),
            `LoD VAF %, median` = round(100 * median(lod_vaf), 2)) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

### Trajectories

```{r lod-stringent-trajectories}
stringent_traj %>%
  group_by(consistency) %>%
  summarise(trajectories = n(),
            variants = n_distinct(variant),
            individuals = n_distinct(ID),
            `timepoints above LoD, mean` = round(mean(n_above), 2),
            `mean VAF %, mean over trajectories` = round(100 * mean(mean_vaf), 3),
            `mean VAF %, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(mean_vaf, 3, 100),
            `lowest VAF of the trajectory %, median` = round(100 * median(min_vaf), 3),
            `highest VAF of the trajectory %, median` = round(100 * median(max_vaf), 3)) %>%
  mutate(`% of trajectories` = round(100 * trajectories / sum(trajectories), 1), .after = trajectories) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

Order of the timepoints above the LoD. A clone that appears and persists is above the LoD from one
timepoint through the last.

```{r lod-stringent-pattern}
# above: is the trajectory above the LoD, timepoints in time order
above_pattern <- function(above) {
  n <- length(above)
  k <- sum(above)
  if (k == n) return("all timepoints")
  if (k == 0) return("no timepoint")
  first <- min(which(above))
  last  <- max(which(above))
  if (last - first + 1 > k) return("intermittent")
  if (last == n) return("from one timepoint through the last")
  if (first == 1) return("from the first timepoint, then lost")
  "one block in between"
}
pattern_levels <- c("all timepoints", "from one timepoint through the last", "from the first timepoint, then lost",
                    "one block in between", "intermittent", "no timepoint")

stringent_traj <- stringent_traj %>%
  left_join(stringent_obs %>%
              arrange(traj_id, LABDATE) %>%
              group_by(traj_id) %>%
              summarise(pattern = above_pattern(status == "VAF >= LoD"), .groups = "drop"),
            by = "traj_id") %>%
  mutate(pattern = factor(pattern, levels = pattern_levels))

stringent_traj %>%
  group_by(pattern) %>%
  summarise(trajectories = n(),
            `timepoints above LoD, median` = median(n_above),
            `Mutect2 calls, median` = median(n_mutect),
            `mean VAF %, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(mean_vaf, 3, 100),
            `highest VAF %, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(max_vaf, 2, 100)) %>%
  mutate(`% of trajectories` = round(100 * trajectories / sum(trajectories), 1), .after = trajectories) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

Every trajectory of the stringent set. One row per trajectory, one column per timepoint of the individual
(samples with foreign DNA left out); number: VAF in %; triangle: Mutect2 call in that sample (filled: `PASS`).

```{r lod-stringent-heatmap, fig.width=9, fig.height=max(4, 0.15 * nrow(stringent_traj) + 2.5)}
stringent_obs %>%
  left_join(stringent_traj %>% select(traj_id, pattern, max_vaf), by = "traj_id") %>%
  left_join(lod_calls %>% transmute(traj_id, Sample, call = ifelse(FILTER == "PASS", "PASS", "other flags")),
            by = c("traj_id", "Sample")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(timepoint), y = fct_reorder(traj_id, max_vaf))) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = status), colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(k > 0, sprintf("%.2f", 100 * vaf), "")), size = 2.2, hjust = 1, nudge_x = 0.38) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = call), size = 1.3, position = position_nudge(x = -0.33), na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = alpha(status_colors, 0.55), drop = FALSE) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("PASS" = 17, "other flags" = 2), na.translate = FALSE, name = "Mutect2 call") +
  facet_grid(pattern ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", labeller = label_wrap_gen(14)) +
  labs(x = "Timepoint of the individual", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6), strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, size = 7),
        legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical")
```

### Other limits for the number of individuals

The same trajectories with a `PASS` call, for other values of `max_individuals` (applied to both counts).

```{r lod-stringent-threshold}
map_dfr(c(1, 2, 5, 10, Inf), function(m) {
  som_all %>%
    filter(n_pass > 0, N_IDs <= m, ids_above_lod <= m) %>%
    summarise(`max_individuals` = ifelse(is.finite(m), as.character(m), "no limit"),
              trajectories = n(),
              variants = n_distinct(variant),
              `all timepoints above LoD` = n_pct(consistency == consistency_levels[1]),
              `some` = n_pct(consistency == consistency_levels[2]),
              `none` = n_pct(consistency == consistency_levels[3]),
              `mean VAF %, all / some / none` = paste(sprintf("%.2f", 100 * tapply(mean_vaf, consistency, mean)), collapse = " / "))
}) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```


## 7.7 Samples with foreign DNA

The same headline numbers with the `r length(mixed_samples)` flagged samples included, for the Mutect2-called
potential somatic trajectories. The class of 4.2 is recalculated with all samples.

```{r lod-sensitivity}
class_all_samples <- full_join(
  mutect_rule(merged_vcf %>% filter(CHIP == 0)),
  readcount_all %>%
    filter(CHIP == 0, longitudinal, depth > 0) %>%
    group_by(ID, variant, traj_id) %>%
    summarise(pileup_median_VAF = median(VAF), .groups = "drop"),
  by = c("ID", "variant", "traj_id")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(class_mutect),
         class_mutect == "potential somatic", !coalesce(pileup_median_VAF >= low_af_max, FALSE))

obs_all_samples <- readcount_all %>%
  filter(traj_id %in% class_all_samples$traj_id, depth > 0,
         type %in% c("SNV", "deletion"), variant %in% pileup_ok_variants) %>%
  transmute(traj_id, n = depth, k = alt_count)

# depths of the flagged samples that are not yet in lod_tab
new_pairs <- obs_all_samples %>% distinct(n, k) %>% anti_join(lod_tab, by = c("n", "k"))
lod_tab_all <- bind_rows(lod_tab, lod_frequentist(n = new_pairs$n, k = new_pairs$k,
                                                 e = err_rate, alpha = alpha, power_target = power_tgt))

headline <- function(obs) {
  obs %>%
    filter(!is.na(lod_vaf)) %>%
    mutate(above = k / n >= lod_vaf) %>%
    group_by(traj_id) %>%
    summarise(timepoints = n(), n_above = sum(above), .groups = "drop") %>%
    summarise(trajectories = n(),
              observations = sum(timepoints),
              `observations above LoD` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", sum(n_above), 100 * sum(n_above) / sum(timepoints)),
              `all timepoints above LoD` = n_pct(n_above == timepoints),
              `some` = n_pct(n_above > 0 & n_above < timepoints),
              `none` = n_pct(n_above == 0))
}

bind_rows(
  lod_obs %>% filter(group == "Mutect2-called, potential somatic") %>% headline() %>%
    mutate(samples = "flagged samples left out (sections 7.2 to 7.6)"),
  obs_all_samples %>% left_join(lod_tab_all, by = c("n", "k")) %>% headline() %>%
    mutate(samples = "all samples")) %>%
  relocate(samples) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```


## 7.8 Summary

```{r lod-headline, include=FALSE}
som <- lod_obs %>% filter(group == "Mutect2-called, potential somatic")
bg  <- lod_obs %>% filter(group == "pileup only, potential somatic")
bg_traj <- lod_traj %>% filter(group == "pileup only, potential somatic")
som_calls <- lod_calls %>%
  filter(class == "potential somatic") %>%
  left_join(nonchip_recurrence %>% select(variant, N_IDs), by = "variant")
all_above <- consistency_levels[1]
pct <- function(x, accuracy = 0.1) percent(x, accuracy = accuracy)
traj_share    <- function(traj, level) pct(mean(traj$consistency == level))
traj_mean_vaf <- function(traj, level) pct(mean(traj$mean_vaf[traj$consistency == level]), 0.01)
```

- **Limit of detection.** Over the `r nrow(lod_obs)` observations (non-CHIP SNVs and deletions at every
  timepoint of the `r n_distinct(lod_obs$ID)` longitudinal individuals) the median depth is
  `r median(lod_obs$n)` and the median LoD is a VAF of `r pct(median(lod_obs$lod_vaf), 0.01)` (IQR
  `r pct(quantile(lod_obs$lod_vaf, 0.25), 0.01)` to `r pct(quantile(lod_obs$lod_vaf, 0.75), 0.01)`, range
  `r pct(min(lod_obs$lod_vaf), 0.01)` to `r pct(max(lod_obs$lod_vaf), 0.01)`), with `k_star` between
  `r min(lod_obs$k_star)` and `r max(lod_obs$k_star)` reads. `r sum(lod_obs$lod_vaf > chip_vaf)` observations
  have a LoD above the CHIP threshold of `r pct(chip_vaf, 1)`.
- **Mutect2 calls.** With Mutect2's own read counts, `r pct(mean(lod_calls$status == "VAF >= LoD"))` of the
  `r nrow(lod_calls)` non-CHIP calls are above the LoD (`r sum(lod_calls$status != "VAF >= LoD")` are not);
  among the potential somatic calls it is
  `r pct(mean(lod_calls$status[lod_calls$class == "potential somatic"] == "VAF >= LoD"))`.
- **Potential somatic variants that Mutect2 called, at all timepoints** (`r nrow(som_traj)` trajectories of
  `r n_distinct(som_traj$variant)` variants): `r pct(mean(som$status == "VAF >= LoD"))` of the `r nrow(som)`
  observations are above the LoD, `r pct(mean(som$status == "called, VAF < LoD"))` are called but below it
  and `r pct(mean(som$status == "not called (k < k*)"))` are not called. Median VAF: 
  `r pct(median(som$vaf[som$status == "VAF >= LoD"]), 0.01)` above the LoD,
  `r pct(median(som$vaf[som$status == "called, VAF < LoD"]), 0.01)` called but below it,
  `r pct(median(som$vaf[som$status == "not called (k < k*)"]), 0.01)` not called.
- **Trajectories of these variants.** `r traj_share(som_traj, consistency_levels[1])` are above the LoD at
  all timepoints (mean VAF of these trajectories `r traj_mean_vaf(som_traj, consistency_levels[1])`),
  `r traj_share(som_traj, consistency_levels[2])` at some timepoints (mean VAF
  `r traj_mean_vaf(som_traj, consistency_levels[2])`) and `r traj_share(som_traj, consistency_levels[3])` at
  none (mean VAF `r traj_mean_vaf(som_traj, consistency_levels[3])`).
- **Which trajectories stay above the LoD.** `r pct(mean(som_traj$N_IDs[som_traj$consistency == all_above] > 20))`
  of the trajectories that are above the LoD at all timepoints belong to the
  `r n_distinct(som_traj$variant[som_traj$N_IDs > 20])` variants that are called in more than 20 individuals.
  Of the `r sum(som_traj$N_IDs == 1)` trajectories of variants called in a single individual,
  `r pct(mean(som_traj$consistency[som_traj$N_IDs == 1] == all_above))` are above the LoD at all timepoints.
- **Stringent set** (trajectories with a `PASS` call of a variant found in at most `r max_individuals`
  individuals, section 7.6; `r nrow(stringent_traj)` trajectories of `r n_distinct(stringent_traj$variant)`
  variants in `r n_distinct(stringent_traj$ID)` individuals): `r pct(mean(stringent_obs$status == "VAF >= LoD"))`
  of the `r nrow(stringent_obs)` observations are above the LoD (median VAF
  `r pct(median(stringent_obs$vaf[stringent_obs$status == "VAF >= LoD"]), 0.01)`),
  `r pct(mean(stringent_obs$status == "called, VAF < LoD"))` are called but below it (median VAF
  `r pct(median(stringent_obs$vaf[stringent_obs$status == "called, VAF < LoD"]), 0.01)`) and
  `r pct(mean(stringent_obs$status == "not called (k < k*)"))` are not called.
  `r traj_share(stringent_traj, consistency_levels[1])` of the trajectories are above the LoD at all timepoints
  (mean VAF `r traj_mean_vaf(stringent_traj, consistency_levels[1])`),
  `r traj_share(stringent_traj, consistency_levels[2])` at some (mean VAF
  `r traj_mean_vaf(stringent_traj, consistency_levels[2])`) and
  `r traj_share(stringent_traj, consistency_levels[3])` at none (mean VAF
  `r traj_mean_vaf(stringent_traj, consistency_levels[3])`).
  `r sum(stringent_traj$pattern == "from one timepoint through the last")` of the
  `r sum(stringent_traj$consistency == consistency_levels[2])` trajectories that are above the LoD at some
  timepoints are above it from one timepoint through the last; `r sum(stringent_traj$n_above == 1)`
  trajectories are above it at a single timepoint.
- **Same sites without a call** (pileup only, potential somatic; `r nrow(bg_traj)` trajectories):
  `r pct(mean(bg$called))` of the observations reach `k_star` and `r pct(mean(bg$status == "VAF >= LoD"))`
  are above the LoD, where sequencing error at rate `e` alone gives at most `r pct(alpha, 1)` that reach
  `k_star`. `r traj_share(bg_traj, consistency_levels[1])` of these trajectories are above the LoD at all
  timepoints. These sites are not a random sample: each one is a site where Mutect2 made a call in another
  individual.

Points to keep in mind when reading these numbers:

- Being above the LoD says that the reads are more than random sequencing error at rate `e`. It does not
  say that the variant is a clone. Of the potential somatic non-CHIP calls,
  `r pct(mean(som_calls$FILTER != "PASS"))` carry Mutect2 filter flags and `r pct(mean(som_calls$N_IDs > 20))`
  belong to variants that are called in more than 20 individuals. This is what a site-specific artefact
  looks like, and such an artefact is above the LoD at every timepoint.
- The error background `e / 3` describes base substitutions with one rate for all sites. The same rule is
  applied to deletions here.
- The pileup counts are not filtered on base quality; Mutect2's counts are.
- `alpha` is a per-site rate, without correction for the number of sites.
- Insertions and multi-nucleotide variants are only in the Mutect2-based table.


# 8. Theoretical LoD and the data (paper figures)

Figures and numbers for the paper, for two cohorts:

- **SHCS**: the CHIP measurements of the paper, `results/SHCS_CHIP_variants_depth_LoD.txt` (written by
  `02_SHCS_CHIP_trajectories.Rmd`): depth and variant reads of every timepoint of every
  trajectory, from the Mutect2 call, from bam-readcount, or not detected (no variant read).
- **SardiNIA**: the trajectories of the analysis (`resources/LoD/sardinia_chip_calls_long_filtered.txt`, written by
  `04_SardiNIA_CHIP_trajectories.Rmd`),
  with the read counts of `ALLvariants_exclSynonymous_Xadj.txt`.
  The variant reads are the raw reads (`TOTALcount - WTcount`); `MUTcount_Xadj` is halved for X-linked variants
  in men.

The four figures and their assembly, Figure S2 (`FigS2_LoD_depth_kstar`), are written to
`output/Supplementary_Figures/` as png and svg when `write_paper_figures` is `TRUE`. The tables are only shown here.

## 8.1 Data

```{r paper-inputs}
# section 8 needs the trajectory tables of both cohorts (02_SHCS_CHIP_trajectories.Rmd, 04_SardiNIA_CHIP_trajectories.Rmd);
# on the first run of the pipeline the notebook stops here, and run_all.R knits it again at the end
paper_inputs <- c("results/SHCS_CHIP_variants_depth_LoD.txt", "resources/LoD/sardinia_chip_calls_long_filtered.txt")
if (!all(file.exists(paper_inputs))) knitr::knit_exit("Section 8 is skipped: the trajectory tables do not exist yet.")
```

```{r paper-data}
source("R/Set_colors.R")                  # hiv_colors: SHCS red, SardiNIA grey
cohort_levels <- c("SHCS", "Sardinia")
cohort_colors <- hiv_colors[cohort_levels]

shcs_meas <- read.delim("results/SHCS_CHIP_variants_depth_LoD.txt") %>%
  transmute(cohort = "SHCS", id = SHCS_ID, traj_id = Trajectory, n = Depth, k = Alt_reads, lod_table = LoD,
            group = recode(Source, "Mutect2" = "Mutect2 call", "bam-readcount" = "variant reads in the pile-up",
                           "imputed" = "not detected (k = 0)"))

sard_set <- read.table("resources/LoD/sardinia_chip_calls_long_filtered.txt", sep = "\t", header = TRUE) %>%
  transmute(SardID = as.integer(sub("Sard_", "", SardID)), CHR = as.character(Chr), START = Start, END = End, REF = Ref, ALT = Alt) %>%
  distinct()

sard_meas <- read.table("resources/SardiNIA/ALLvariants_exclSynonymous_Xadj.txt", sep = "\t", header = TRUE) %>%
  filter(!is.na(TOTALcount)) %>%
  semi_join(sard_set, by = c("SardID", "CHR", "START", "END", "REF", "ALT")) %>%
  transmute(cohort = "Sardinia", id = paste0("Sard_", SardID), traj_id = paste(id, Gene, CHR, START, REF, ALT, sep = ":"),
            n = TOTALcount, k = TOTALcount - WTcount, lod_table = NA_real_,
            group = ifelse(k > 0, "variant reads (k >= 1)", "not detected (k = 0)"))

# measurements of the CHIP clones and of the stringent non-CHIP set with a Mutect2 VCF (for section 8.4)
detection_obs <- bind_rows(
  readcount_all %>%
    filter(CHIP == 1, longitudinal, has_vcf, !S_ID %in% mixed_samples, depth > 0, type %in% c("SNV", "deletion")) %>%
    group_by(traj_id) %>%
    filter(sum(Detected) > 0) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    transmute(set = "CHIP clones", traj_id, n = depth, k = alt_count, Detected),
  stringent_obs %>%
    filter(has_vcf) %>%
    transmute(set = "non-CHIP, stringent set", traj_id, n, k, Detected))

# k*, called and LoD of every measurement; lod_tab (section 7) already has many of the (n, k) pairs
new_pairs <- bind_rows(shcs_meas, sard_meas, detection_obs) %>%
  distinct(n, k) %>%
  anti_join(lod_tab, by = c("n", "k"))
lod_tab_paper <- bind_rows(lod_tab, lod_frequentist(n = new_pairs$n, k = new_pairs$k,
                                                    e = err_rate, alpha = alpha, power_target = power_tgt))
add_lod_paper <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    left_join(lod_tab_paper %>% select(n, k, k_star, called, lod_vaf), by = c("n", "k")) %>%
    mutate(vaf = k / n)
}

cohort_meas   <- add_lod_paper(bind_rows(shcs_meas, sard_meas)) %>%
  mutate(cohort = factor(cohort, levels = cohort_levels),
         group  = factor(group, levels = c("Mutect2 call", "variant reads in the pile-up", "variant reads (k >= 1)", "not detected (k = 0)")))
detection_obs <- add_lod_paper(detection_obs)

# the LoD in the SHCS table is the same calculation (rounded there)
stopifnot(!anyNA(cohort_meas$lod_vaf),
          all(abs(cohort_meas$lod_table - cohort_meas$lod_vaf) / cohort_meas$lod_vaf < 0.01, na.rm = TRUE))

cohort_meas %>%
  group_by(cohort, group) %>%
  summarise(measurements = n(), individuals = n_distinct(id), trajectories = n_distinct(traj_id), .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

Error background in SHCS: CHIP positions in the samples of individuals who carry nothing there (no Mutect2
call and no allele at 1% or more at that position), without the samples with foreign DNA (section 3.3) and
without any site where a non-reference base reaches 1%. Each site gives three (site, alternate base) pairs,
with `k` the reads of that base. There is no such background for SardiNIA, whose table only has the carriers.

```{r paper-background}
carrier_pos <- readcount_all %>%
  filter(Detected == 1 | VAF >= 0.01) %>%
  distinct(ID, chr, pos)

background_pairs <- pileup_sites %>%
  semi_join(readcount_chip %>% distinct(chr, pos), by = c("chr", "pos")) %>%
  inner_join(samples %>% filter(ID %in% long_ids) %>% select(Sample, ID), by = c("S_ID" = "Sample")) %>%
  filter(!S_ID %in% mixed_samples, depth > 0) %>%
  anti_join(carrier_pos, by = c("ID", "chr", "pos")) %>%
  crossing(allele = c("A", "C", "G", "T")) %>%
  filter(allele != ref) %>%
  left_join(pileup_alleles, by = c("S_ID", "chr", "pos", "allele")) %>%
  mutate(k = replace_na(count, 0L)) %>%
  group_by(S_ID, chr, pos) %>%
  filter(max(k / depth) < 0.01) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  transmute(S_ID, ID, chr, pos, substitution = paste0(ref, ">", allele), n = depth, k)

# k* at each depth, and the share of error-only sites that the model expects to reach it
background_kstar <- tibble(n = unique(background_pairs$n)) %>%
  mutate(k_star = map_int(n, function(n) chip_lod$k_star(n, err_rate, alpha)),
         fp_model = map2_dbl(k_star, n, function(ks, n) chip_lod$pvalue(ks, n, err_rate)))
background_pairs <- background_pairs %>% left_join(background_kstar, by = "n")

c(pairs = nrow(background_pairs), positions = nrow(distinct(background_pairs, chr, pos)),
  samples = n_distinct(background_pairs$S_ID), individuals = n_distinct(background_pairs$ID))
```

Theoretical `k*` and LoD over depth, for the error rate used (`e = 0.001`) and for half and twice that rate.
`k*` is calculated for every depth, the LoD on a grid of depths and on both sides of every step of `k*`.

```{r paper-theory}
e_curves    <- c(err_rate / 2, err_rate, 2 * err_rate)
depth_range <- c(100, 8000)

# k* never decreases with depth, so each search starts at the k* of the previous depth
theory_kstar <- map_dfr(e_curves, function(e) {
  n  <- depth_range[1]:depth_range[2]
  ks <- integer(length(n))
  k  <- 0L
  for (i in seq_along(n)) {
    while (chip_lod$pvalue(k, n[i], e) > alpha) k <- k + 1L
    ks[i] <- k
  }
  tibble(e = e, n = n, k_star = ks)
})

theory_steps <- theory_kstar %>%
  group_by(e) %>%
  filter(k_star != lag(k_star)) %>%
  ungroup()

theory_lod <- bind_rows(
  expand_grid(e = e_curves, n = c(unique(round(10^seq(log10(depth_range[1]), log10(depth_range[2]), length.out = 150))),
                                  500, 1000, 2000, 3000)),
  theory_steps %>% select(e, n),
  theory_steps %>% transmute(e, n = n - 1)) %>%
  mutate(n = as.integer(n)) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  filter(n >= depth_range[1]) %>%
  left_join(theory_kstar, by = c("e", "n")) %>%
  mutate(lod_vaf = pmap_dbl(list(n, e, k_star), function(n, e, ks) chip_lod$lod_vaf(n, e, alpha, power_tgt, ks))) %>%
  arrange(e, n)

e_label  <- function(e) factor(paste("e =", format(e, scientific = FALSE, drop0trailing = TRUE)),
                               levels = paste("e =", format(e_curves, scientific = FALSE, drop0trailing = TRUE)))
e_lines  <- setNames(c("dotted", "solid", "dashed"), levels(e_label(e_curves)))
theory_kstar <- theory_kstar %>% mutate(e_lab = e_label(e))
theory_lod   <- theory_lod %>% mutate(e_lab = e_label(e))

# the points a step line needs: first and last depth, and every depth at which k* changes
step_points <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    group_by(e) %>%
    filter(row_number() == 1 | row_number() == n() | k_star != lag(k_star)) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# depths at which k* (e = 0.001) goes up by one read
theory_steps %>% filter(e == err_rate) %>% transmute(depth = n, k_star) %>% knitr::kable()
```


## 8.2 Theoretical k* and LoD over depth

Lines: theory for three error rates. Shaded: interquartile range of the depth of the measurements of each cohort.
Margins: depth of the measurements (top) and their `k*` or LoD at `e = 0.001` (right). `k*` takes whole
values, so its margin shows the share of measurements at each value instead of a density.

```{r paper-figure-helpers}
paper_theme  <- theme_classic(base_size = 11)
margin_theme <- theme_void() + theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))

# main plot with a density margin on top and on the right, legends of the main plot on the right
with_margins <- function(main, top, right) {
  top + plot_spacer() + main + right +
    plot_layout(ncol = 2, widths = c(4, 1), heights = c(1, 4), guides = "collect")
}

save_paper_figure <- function(plot, name, width = 7, height = 5) {
  if (!write_paper_figures) return(invisible(NULL))
  dir.create(paper_fig_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  for (ext in c("png", "svg")) {
    ggsave(file.path(paper_fig_dir, paste0(name, ".", ext)), plot, width = width, height = height, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  }
}

depth_scale <- scale_x_log10(limits = depth_range, breaks = c(100, 300, 1000, 3000))
cohort_labels <- c(SHCS = "SHCS", Sardinia = "SardiNIA")
cohort_fill   <- scale_fill_manual(values = cohort_colors, labels = cohort_labels, name = "Cohort\n(depth IQR)")
cohort_colour <- scale_colour_manual(values = cohort_colors, guide = "none")

depth_iqr <- cohort_meas %>%
  group_by(cohort) %>%
  summarise(lo = quantile(n, 0.25), hi = quantile(n, 0.75), .groups = "drop")

p_depth_margin <- ggplot(cohort_meas, aes(n, fill = cohort, colour = cohort)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.3) +
  depth_scale + cohort_colour +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cohort_colors, guide = "none") +
  margin_theme
```

```{r paper-figure-kstar, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
kstar_max <- max(theory_kstar$k_star)

p_kstar <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = depth_iqr, aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = cohort), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_step(data = step_points(theory_kstar), aes(n, k_star, linetype = e_lab), linewidth = 0.5) +
  depth_scale +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.5, kstar_max + 0.5), breaks = 1:kstar_max) +
  cohort_fill +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = e_lines, name = "Error rate") +
  labs(x = "Depth at the variant site", y = "k* (variant reads needed)") +
  paper_theme

# share of the measurements at each k*, the two cohorts side by side
p_kstar_margin <- cohort_meas %>%
  count(cohort, k_star, name = "measurements") %>%
  group_by(cohort) %>%
  mutate(share = measurements / sum(measurements),
         offset = ifelse(cohort == "SHCS", -0.18, 0.18)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(xmin = 0, xmax = share, ymin = k_star + offset - 0.16, ymax = k_star + offset + 0.16, fill = cohort)) +
  geom_rect(alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.5, kstar_max + 0.5)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cohort_colors, guide = "none") +
  margin_theme

fig_kstar <- with_margins(p_kstar, p_depth_margin, p_kstar_margin)
fig_kstar
save_paper_figure(fig_kstar, "LoD_theory_kstar_vs_depth")
```

```{r paper-figure-lod, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
lod_lim   <- range(c(theory_lod$lod_vaf, cohort_meas$lod_vaf))
lod_scale <- scale_y_log10(limits = lod_lim,
                           breaks = c(0.001, 0.002, 0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05), labels = label_percent(accuracy = 0.1))

p_lod <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = depth_iqr, aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi, ymin = lod_lim[1], ymax = lod_lim[2], fill = cohort), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(data = theory_lod, aes(n, lod_vaf, linetype = e_lab), linewidth = 0.5) +
  depth_scale + lod_scale +
  cohort_fill +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = e_lines, name = "Error rate") +
  labs(x = "Depth at the variant site", y = "LoD (VAF)") +
  paper_theme

p_lod_margin <- ggplot(cohort_meas, aes(y = lod_vaf, fill = cohort, colour = cohort)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.3) +
  lod_scale + cohort_colour +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cohort_colors, guide = "none") +
  margin_theme

fig_lod <- with_margins(p_lod, p_depth_margin, p_lod_margin)
fig_lod
save_paper_figure(fig_lod, "LoD_theory_LoD_vs_depth")
```


## 8.3 Measurements against k*

Each point is one measurement: its depth and its number of variant reads. Line: `k*` at `e = 0.001`, the reads
needed for a call. Margins: density of depth (top) and of variant reads (right) for each group of
measurements; the read densities use a narrow bandwidth on the log scale and are scaled to the same height,
so that the measurements without a variant read show as a peak at 0. In SHCS the grey points are the error background (section 8.1; a random sample of 15,000 of
the pairs within the depth range of the measurements, drawn with a small vertical jitter). Colours are the R
defaults.

```{r paper-figure-reads-helper}
reads_scale <- function(max_k) {
  scale_y_continuous(trans = pseudo_log_trans(sigma = 1, base = 10), limits = c(-0.4, max_k * 1.15),
                     breaks = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000))
}

# meas: n, k, group; background: n, k (optional)
plot_reads_vs_kstar <- function(meas, group_levels, background = NULL, background_label = NULL) {
  meas <- meas %>% mutate(group = factor(group, levels = group_levels))
  group_cols <- setNames(hue_pal()(length(group_levels)), group_levels)     # R's default colours
  depth_lim  <- range(meas$n) * c(0.95, 1.05)
  x_scale    <- scale_x_log10(limits = depth_lim)
  y_scale    <- reads_scale(max(meas$k))
  kline      <- step_points(theory_kstar %>% filter(e == err_rate, n >= depth_lim[1], n <= depth_lim[2]))

  main <- ggplot()
  if (!is.null(background)) {
    main <- main + geom_point(data = background, aes(n, k_jitter, colour = background_label), size = 0.3, alpha = 0.35)
  }
  point_cols <- group_cols
  if (!is.null(background)) point_cols[background_label] <- "grey65"
  main <- main +
    geom_step(data = kline, aes(n, k_star, linetype = paste0("k* (e = ", err_rate, ")")), linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_point(data = meas, aes(n, k, colour = group), size = 1.2, alpha = 0.85) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = point_cols, breaks = names(point_cols), name = NULL) +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = "solid", name = NULL) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2.2, alpha = 1), order = 1),
           linetype = guide_legend(order = 2)) +
    x_scale + y_scale +
    labs(x = "Depth at the variant site", y = "Variant reads (k)") +
    paper_theme

  top <- ggplot(meas, aes(n, fill = group, colour = group)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.3) +
    x_scale +
    scale_fill_manual(values = group_cols, guide = "none") + scale_colour_manual(values = group_cols, guide = "none") +
    margin_theme

  # a narrow bandwidth (log scale) keeps the "k = 0" group at 0; each group is scaled to its own peak
  right <- ggplot(meas, aes(y = k, x = after_stat(scaled), fill = group, colour = group)) +
    geom_density(alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.3, bw = 0.08) +
    y_scale +
    scale_fill_manual(values = group_cols, guide = "none") + scale_colour_manual(values = group_cols, guide = "none") +
    margin_theme

  with_margins(main, top, right)
}
```

SHCS:

                                      group_levels = c("Mutect2 call", "variant reads in the pile-up", "not detected (k = 0)"),
                                      background = background_plot,
                                      background_label = "background (no variant expected)")
fig_reads_shcs

## 8.4 Numbers for the text

### LoD of the measurements

```{r paper-table-lod}
cohort_meas %>%
  group_by(cohort) %>%
  summarise(measurements = n(),
            individuals = n_distinct(id),
            trajectories = n_distinct(traj_id),
            `depth, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(n),
            `depth, range` = paste(range(n), collapse = "-"),
            `k*: share of measurements` = paste(sprintf("%d: %.1f%%", as.integer(names(table(k_star))),
                                                        100 * prop.table(table(k_star))), collapse = ", "),
            `LoD VAF %, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(lod_vaf, 2, 100),
            `LoD VAF %, range` = paste(round(100 * range(lod_vaf), 2), collapse = "-"),
            `LoD <= 0.5%` = percent(mean(lod_vaf <= 0.005), accuracy = 0.1),
            `LoD <= 1%` = percent(mean(lod_vaf <= 0.01), accuracy = 0.1)) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

### Measurements against k* and the LoD

```{r paper-table-measurements}
cohort_meas %>%
  group_by(cohort, group) %>%
  summarise(measurements = n(),
            `k = 0` = n_pct(k == 0),
            `0 < k < k*` = n_pct(k > 0 & !called),
            `k >= k* (called)` = n_pct(called),
            `VAF >= LoD` = n_pct(vaf >= lod_vaf),
            `variant reads, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(k),
            `VAF %, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(vaf, 2, 100),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

### Error background against the model (SHCS)

```{r paper-table-background}
e_fit <- 3 * sum(background_pairs$k) / sum(background_pairs$n)
e_ci  <- 3 * c(qchisq(0.025, 2 * sum(background_pairs$k)) / 2, qchisq(0.975, 2 * (sum(background_pairs$k) + 1)) / 2) /
  sum(background_pairs$n)

tibble(`(site, base) pairs` = nrow(background_pairs),
       positions = nrow(distinct(background_pairs, chr, pos)),
       samples = n_distinct(background_pairs$S_ID),
       `depth, median (IQR)` = med_iqr(background_pairs$n),
       `e used` = err_rate,
       `e estimated, 3 x reads / depth (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.5f (%.5f-%.5f)", e_fit, e_ci[1], e_ci[2]),
       `k >= k*, observed` = percent(mean(background_pairs$k >= background_pairs$k_star), accuracy = 0.01),
       `k >= k*, expected by the model` = percent(mean(background_pairs$fp_model), accuracy = 0.01),
       alpha = percent(alpha)) %>%
  knitr::kable()

# distribution of the reads of a background pair: observed, and Poisson with the e used and with the estimated e
k_levels <- c(as.character(0:5), ">= 6")
pois_share <- function(e) {
  lambda <- background_pairs$n * e / 3
  c(sapply(0:5, function(j) mean(dpois(j, lambda))), mean(ppois(5, lambda, lower.tail = FALSE)))
}
tibble(`variant reads` = k_levels,
       `observed %` = round(100 * c(sapply(0:5, function(j) mean(background_pairs$k == j)), mean(background_pairs$k >= 6)), 3),
       `Poisson, e used %` = round(100 * pois_share(err_rate), 3),
       `Poisson, e estimated %` = round(100 * pois_share(e_fit), 3)) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

By substitution (with 95% Poisson interval):

```{r paper-table-substitution}
background_pairs %>%
  group_by(substitution) %>%
  summarise(pairs = n(),
            `k >= k*` = percent(mean(k >= k_star), accuracy = 0.1),
            reads = sum(k),
            depth = sum(n),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(e = 3 * reads / depth,
         lo = 3 * qchisq(0.025, 2 * reads) / 2 / depth,
         hi = 3 * qchisq(0.975, 2 * (reads + 1)) / 2 / depth) %>%
  arrange(-e) %>%
  transmute(substitution, pairs, `e estimated (95% CI)` = sprintf("%.5f (%.5f-%.5f)", e, lo, hi), `k >= k*`) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

### Detection by Mutect2 against the LoD (SHCS)

Measurements of variants that are present in the individual (CHIP clones with a Mutect2 call, and the
stringent non-CHIP set of section 7.6), in samples with a Mutect2 VCF: share called by Mutect2, by the pileup
VAF relative to the LoD at that depth (95% exact binomial interval).

```{r paper-table-mutect2}
detection_obs %>%
  mutate(ratio = vaf / lod_vaf,
         `VAF / LoD` = ifelse(k == 0, "no variant read", as.character(cut(ratio, c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 5, 10, Inf))))) %>%
  arrange(ratio) %>%
  mutate(`VAF / LoD` = fct_inorder(`VAF / LoD`)) %>%
  group_by(set, `VAF / LoD`) %>%
  summarise(measurements = n(), called = sum(Detected == 1), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(ci = map2(called, measurements, function(x, n) binom.test(x, n)$conf.int),
         `called by Mutect2` = sprintf("%.1f%% (%.1f-%.1f)", 100 * called / measurements,
                                       100 * map_dbl(ci, 1), 100 * map_dbl(ci, 2))) %>%
  select(-ci, -called) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = set, values_from = c(measurements, `called by Mutect2`), names_glue = "{set}: {.value}") %>%
  knitr::kable()
```

### Summary

```{r paper-summary-values, include=FALSE}
shcs_m <- cohort_meas %>% filter(cohort == "SHCS")
sard_m <- cohort_meas %>% filter(cohort == "Sardinia")
pct_k  <- function(x, value) percent(mean(x == value), accuracy = 0.1)
det_r  <- detection_obs %>% filter(set == "CHIP clones") %>% mutate(r = vaf / lod_vaf)
```

- **Theory.** At `e = 0.001` and `alpha = 0.05`, `k*` is 2 variant reads from a depth of
  `r theory_steps$n[theory_steps$e == err_rate & theory_steps$k_star == 2]`, 3 from
  `r theory_steps$n[theory_steps$e == err_rate & theory_steps$k_star == 3]` and 4 from `r theory_steps$n[theory_steps$e == err_rate & theory_steps$k_star == 4]`.
  The LoD falls with depth, from
  `r percent(theory_lod$lod_vaf[theory_lod$e == err_rate & theory_lod$n == 1000], accuracy = 0.01)` at depth 1,000 to
  `r percent(theory_lod$lod_vaf[theory_lod$e == err_rate & theory_lod$n == 2000], accuracy = 0.01)` at 2,000 (table below).
- **SHCS.** The `r nrow(shcs_m)` measurements of the `r n_distinct(shcs_m$traj_id)` CHIP trajectories have a median
  depth of `r median(shcs_m$n)` (IQR `r round(quantile(shcs_m$n, 0.25))`-`r round(quantile(shcs_m$n, 0.75))`); `k*` is 3 reads for
  `r pct_k(shcs_m$k_star, 3)` of them and the median LoD is `r percent(median(shcs_m$lod_vaf), accuracy = 0.01)`
  (range `r percent(min(shcs_m$lod_vaf), accuracy = 0.01)`-`r percent(max(shcs_m$lod_vaf), accuracy = 0.01)`).
- **SardiNIA.** The `r nrow(sard_m)` measurements of the `r n_distinct(sard_m$traj_id)` trajectories have a median
  depth of `r median(sard_m$n)` (IQR `r round(quantile(sard_m$n, 0.25))`-`r round(quantile(sard_m$n, 0.75))`) and a median LoD of
  `r percent(median(sard_m$lod_vaf), accuracy = 0.01)` (range `r percent(min(sard_m$lod_vaf), accuracy = 0.01)`-`r percent(max(sard_m$lod_vaf), accuracy = 0.01)`).
- **Measurements against k\*.** In SHCS `r sum(shcs_m$group == "Mutect2 call" & shcs_m$vaf >= shcs_m$lod_vaf)` of the
  `r sum(shcs_m$group == "Mutect2 call")` Mutect2 measurements are above the LoD; of the `r sum(shcs_m$group == "variant reads in the pile-up")` measurements from bam-readcount,
  `r sum(shcs_m$group == "variant reads in the pile-up" & shcs_m$called)` reach `k*` and
  `r sum(shcs_m$group == "variant reads in the pile-up" & shcs_m$vaf >= shcs_m$lod_vaf)` are above the LoD. In SardiNIA
  `r percent(mean(sard_m$vaf >= sard_m$lod_vaf), accuracy = 0.1)` of the measurements are above the LoD and
  `r sum(sard_m$k == 0)` have no variant read.
- **Error background.** At `r format(nrow(background_pairs), big.mark = ",")` (site, base) pairs at CHIP positions
  where no variant is expected, the error rate estimated from the reads is `r sprintf("%.5f", e_fit)`, against
  `r err_rate` used, and `r percent(mean(background_pairs$k >= background_pairs$k_star), accuracy = 0.1)` of the pairs
  reach `k*` (`r percent(mean(background_pairs$fp_model), accuracy = 0.1)` expected by the model, at most
  `r percent(alpha)` by construction). The counts are more dispersed than Poisson: the error rate differs between
  substitutions (table above).
- **Detection by Mutect2.** Of the CHIP clone measurements with a VAF below the LoD, Mutect2 called
  `r sum(det_r$Detected[det_r$r < 1])` of `r sum(det_r$r < 1)`; with a VAF of 5 times the LoD or more it called
  `r percent(mean(det_r$Detected[det_r$r >= 5] == 1), accuracy = 0.1)`.

```{r paper-summary-lod-points}
theory_lod %>%
  filter(e == err_rate, n %in% c(500, 1000, 2000, 3000)) %>%
  transmute(depth = n, k_star, `LoD VAF %` = round(100 * lod_vaf, 3)) %>%
  knitr::kable()
```


# 9. Differences from an earlier version of this notebook

The plots and tables of an earlier version of this notebook are reproduced. Where the result is not identical, the
reason is one of the following.

1. **Alternate read count of Mutect2.** The earlier version took the first value of `AD` for both `ref_count` and
   `alt_count`. `alt_count` is now the second value. No plot of the earlier version used it; section 7.3 does.
2. **CHIP flag.** Same rule (position within 1 bp). The three merges and the removal of duplicates are
   replaced by a direct test, with the same flag for every call. Annotation columns of the Vanderbilt table
   are not carried along, except the gene.
3. **Duplicated pileup rows.** Overlapping regions list some positions more than once per sample. The
   earlier version counted these rows two to sixteen times in `readcount_nonchip_long`; they are now removed. This
   changes `sd_VAF`, the CV threshold and the tables of stable trajectories.
4. **Individuals with a single sample.** The pileup also contains individuals with one sample. They are kept
   in `readcount_all`, but the missed-timepoint tables (section 6.2) use the longitudinal individuals only.
   The last table of that section shows the difference.
5. **The sample piled up twice.** Its two pileup runs carry suffixed names, did not match the manifest and
   formed an individual `NA` in the earlier version. One of the runs is now used as this sample (section 3.1), so
   individual SHCS_40 has all six timepoints in the pileup. The pileup-based plots of this individual have
   one timepoint more than in the earlier version.
6. **Mutect2 against bam-readcount (section 5.1).** The earlier version matched on individual, chromosome,
   position and date, using the table before duplicates were removed. That pairs different alleles at one
   position, repeats some calls and loses the deletions (VCF and pileup positions differ). Calls are now
   matched on sample and exact variant.
7. **Detected against not detected (section 5.2).** The last two chunks of the earlier version used
   `readcount_variants`, which was not defined anywhere in it, so they stopped with an error. It is
   rebuilt here as all variants in all samples with a Mutect2 VCF, with `Detected` for CHIP and non-CHIP
   variants and zero counts included. The summary table and tests of that section are on this table (the
   earlier version used the CHIP rows with at least one read, in all pileup samples).
8. **Region lists.** Not written unless `write_region_files` is `TRUE`, with the corrected insertion
   position and under new file names.
9. **Smaller changes.** `ylim()` followed by `scale_y_log10()` had no effect in the earlier version and is
   dropped; the AF boxplot uses `coord_cartesian()` so that the box is computed on all values; individuals
   without CHIP are derived instead of hard-coded; all plots use `theme_classic()`.

New in this version: the table of filter flags (1.1), exact against position-based CHIP (2.2), recurrence
of non-CHIP variants (2.2), samples with foreign DNA (3.3), the pileup check of the germline split (4.2),
non-CHIP calls and the agreement per variant in the Mutect2 against bam-readcount comparison (5.1), the fits
of AF against depth as numbers (6.1), the missed-timepoint plot (6.2), and sections 7 and 8.
